gloss_en: simchat ha-mitzvot — the joy in performing the commandments, through which (with yirah) one can discern whether a heavenly decree has been sealed (Rabbah bar bar Chana's ship-and-arrow allegory)

the action of pacing to and fro within one's house — Elisha's walking 'once this way and once that way' (II Kings 4:35), likened to the lung's wings fanning the heart, an act with power to revive the dead
yakhol lehachayot metim — the power to resurrect/revive the dead, achieved through pacing back and forth like Elisha reviving the Shunamite's son (II Kings 4)

canonical_he: כשעיניו מאירות וצופות, בבחינות שדה צופים
gloss_en: the state of the field-master's eyes shining and watching — the tzaddik's illuminated vision when souls do God's will, the aspect of 'Sedeh Tzofim,' the field of watchers/seers (Numbers 23:14)
forms: כשעיניו מאירות וצופות, בבחינות שדה צופים

gloss_en: the qualification to pray before the amud — fitness to serve as sheliach tzibbur (prayer leader), earned by gathering the good points in every Jew, even Jewish sinners, into melodies

tasting sweetness in prayer — the capacity to sense sweetness in the words of tefillah, the aspect of 'all my bones shall say' (Ps 35:10), lost by one who blemishes the brit (whose prayer the 'dog' devours)
one who enters into the joy — the person who, entering the joy of the mitzvot, can thereby discern whether a decree is before or after sealing and on which limb of the 'stature' it falls
chokhmah in its proper standing and completeness — wisdom whole and intact, the state of 'one against two,' enabling one to wage God's wars ('wisdom is better than weapons of war,' Eccl 9:18)
waging the wars of Hashem — the capacity to fight God's battles through perfected wisdom rather than weapons, subduing adversaries who pursue the weak of Israel

canonical_he: יכול ללמד לתלמידים חכמתו, ולא יזיק להם.
gloss_en: teaching students without harming them — the ability to transmit one's wisdom safely to disciples, achieved by measuring out one's words with mishpat ('sustains his words with judgment')
forms: יכול ללמד לתלמידים חכמתו, ולא יזיק להם.

gloss_en: the state of having bitachon and giving tzedakah — trust in God ('trust in Hashem and do good,' Ps 37:3) that enables proper charity, which in turn forms perfected speech

turning chirping-sounds into speech — the power to transform inarticulate voice/chirps (tziftzufim) into articulate holy words, effected through tzedakah born of bitachon ('by your mouth — this is charity')
receiving the holiness of Yom Tov — the capacity to sense festival sanctity, gained through attachment to the tzaddik who is himself the aspect of the festival's holiness

seeing one's own lowliness (leading to complete teshuvah) — the Shabbat-enabled vision of one's shiflut, since ShaBaT = shin (three colors of the eye) + bat (pupil), 'See that God has given you the Shabbat'

canonical_he: יכול לשפך לבו כמים לפני ה
gloss_en: pouring out one's heart like water before Hashem — the nighttime hitbodedut of conversing with one's heart and searching one's spirit ('I recall my melody at night... my spirit searches,' Ps 77)
forms: יכול לשפך לבו כמים לפני ה

gloss_en: the Torah's receiving from Chokhmah Ila'ah — Torah's capacity to draw from Supernal Wisdom ('Torah issues from Chokhmah Ila'ah'), possible only when Torah is complete via the Oral Torah
drawing down the shefa — the capacity to bring down divine abundance, tied to revealing God's Kingship whereby the kelipot are subdued beneath the Shekhinah

canonical_he: יכולים לקרב ולהוכיח את מי שצריכין להוכיח
gloss_en: the ability to draw near and rebuke those needing rebuke — fitness to admonish and bring people close, tied to studying Torah aloud with the mouth (calling the Life of life by name)
forms: יכולים לקרב ולהוכיח את מי שצריכין להוכיח

gloss_en: speaking words in holiness — the power to utter holy speech through shalom, which joins the opposites Chasadim and Gevurot, the aspect of Yosef and mesirat nefesh for kiddush Hashem
bringing our mishpat to light — the power, via emunat chakhamim (faith in the Sages, 'do not deviate right or left'), to issue judgment along the central pillar, the balanced middle path

drawing down the holiness of Eretz Yisrael in exile — the capacity to reveal the Land of Israel's kedushah even under the Sitra Achra in bitter galut ('even also this, in the land of their enemies,' Lev 26:41)
earning money legitimately — the capacity to gain wealth only by traversing and breaking the 140 'voices' of the craving for money, since abundance flows from truth

canonical_he: יכולין לקבל רוח נבואה, רוח הקדש
gloss_en: receiving ruach nevuah / ruach ha-kodesh — the capacity to receive the spirit of prophecy/holy spirit, via the musician's hand separating the good spirit from the melancholy evil spirit (as with Elisha's minstrel)
forms: יכולין לקבל רוח נבואה, רוח הקדש

gloss_en: being included in the air of Eretz Yisrael — incorporation into the avira de-Eretz Yisrael, the holy sinless breath (like the breath of schoolchildren) through which the patriarchs are revealed and judgment repelled
subduing and casting down all the enemies — the overthrow of all opposing foes (as the 'great mountain' before Zerubavel), 'not by might nor by power but by My spirit' (Zech 4:6-7)
Yam shel Shlomo — the molten Sea of Solomon in the Temple standing on twelve oxen, symbol of Malkhut/the God-fearing woman resting on the twelve tribes of God (Zohar Vayechi 241)
yamim — 'days' as a symbol for the middot (divine attributes/measures), the vessels bounding the life-force, per 'the measure of my days, what it is' (Ps 39:5)
shefa ruchaniyut — spiritual abundance, the 'right hand' of the Torah ('length of days in her right hand,' Prov 3:16), flowing to the world that is entirely long, the upper worlds
yemina — the kabbalistic Right side (Chesed), Aharon's side in the Korach dispute, unified with the left through hand-clapping

canonical_he: ימצא השם יתברך בין בטיבו בין בעקו
forms: ימצא השם יתברך בין בטיבו בין בעקו

canonical_he: צדיקים שנקראו גם כן ברית שלום
forms: צדיקים שנקראו גם כן ברית שלום

gloss_en: ve-hatznea — 'and [walk] humbly' (Micah 6:8) read as the sefirah Yesod, the third sukkah-wall of 'even a handbreadth,' which 'reveals a tefach and conceals a tefach'
tefach — the handbreadth measure: the sukkah's minimal third wall (Sukkah 6b) symbolizing Yesod, which 'reveals a handbreadth and conceals a handbreadth'
melichut — saltiness, the quality that causes thirst, identified with yissurin/sufferings ('a covenant is said of salt and a covenant is said of sufferings,' Berakhot 5a)
yissurin — sufferings/afflictions as a covenantal category likened to salt (Berakhot 5a), whose felt burning is the soul's thirst, cooled by Torah innovations
yasir mimenu orlat lev — the removal of the 'foreskin of the heart' (spiritual blockage), effected by wisdom-speech awakening the heart
yasir me'alav kol ha-pechadim — the removal of all fears from oneself, achieved by self-judgment (mishpat) of one's affairs
dibburei emet — words/utterances of truth issuing from the tzaddik's thanksgiving, identified with Yaakov and the sefirah Tiferet
temimei darekh — 'the wholesome of way' (Ps. 119:1), epithet for those who gaze upon the inner intellect, linked to Yaakov ish tam
attaining an ever-greater comprehension (hasagah yeteirah) of Divinity — each new level of perception in the World to Come
doing teshuvah upon one's previous comprehension — repenting of the earlier, now-inadequate perception of God after attaining a higher one
Yitzchak and Yishmael, Yaakov and Esav — the four descendants of Avraham corresponding to the Haggadah's Four Sons and the four kingdoms in holiness
middat ha-din — the divine attribute of strict judgment, here identified as the root/aspect of the yetzer hara
gala — the 'wave' in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's ship tale (Bava Batra 73a), symbol of the yetzer hara that seeks to sink Israel's worth
yerei Elokim — 'God-fearer,' the fear-of-God quality defining Malkhut of holiness (as opposed to Malkhut of the Sitra Achra)
damim u-gevurot — the blood and severities (gevurot) released in childbirth, embodying the aspect of yirah (fear)
oznayim — the ears as the organ upon which yirah (fear of God) depends ('fear hangs on the ears,' Tikkun 70), enabling perfected holy speech
ba-keseh — 'at the covered/appointed time' (Ps. 81:4), expounded as kisse/concealment: hidden fear-of-God given over to the heart, root of glory
contemplation by the intellect of God's greatness and exaltedness — the higher fear (yirat ha-romemut) arising from knowing He is great and sovereign
the 'first' (higher) fear — yirah stemming directly from God's greatness and exaltedness, above fear reached via lower frights
tzaddikei ha-dor — the righteous leaders of the generation, sole conduits through whom fear and love of God are received
fear ascending out of the kelipah and the nations — yirah fallen into lowly frights (beasts, officials) being raised back to holy fear via self-judgment
shiflut — lowliness, making oneself like dust (afar), whose 'drawing power' attracts Godliness; why God desired Israel's self-diminishment
pogmin b'Malkhut — blemishing the sefirah of Malkhut, the sin that empowers Peor/Sitra Achra to 'open its mouth'

canonical_he: יש לו כח לפער פיו בצרופים רעים
gloss_en: Peor's power to open its mouth with evil letter-combinations (tzerufim ra'im) — the Sitra Achra's corrupt speech enabled by blemished Malkhut
forms: יש לו כח לפער פיו בצרופים רעים

gloss_en: peace below (shalom l'matah) — the state following revelation of the Covenant of Peace after breaking the orlah, which arouses peace above
yeshut v'taharah — 'existence and purity,' the post-Creation state symbolized by pure marble (shayish tahor) in the Pardes account
completing and erecting the structure of prayer — the tzaddikim of each generation raising seemingly unanswered prayers and building the full stature (like Moshe erecting the Mishkan)
avodat ha-Torah — the service of Torah study, ranked above commerce; the 'Yissachar in your tents' vocation
'Yissachar b'ohalekha' — the blessing-phrase (cf. Deut. 33:18) denoting Yissachar the tent-dwelling Torah scholar, counterpart to Zevulun's commerce

The counsel to ensure that the utterances (dibburim, spoken words — not devorim, bees) leave one's mouth in truth, i.e., speaking truthfully so that God will yearn to dwell with the speaker (Likutey Moharan I:9)
God's yearning from above to dwell with you — the Holy One's desire, drawn solely to truth, to make His dwelling with the truthful person (the ark's 'amah from above')
the nullification of the kelipot (husks of impurity) — their annihilation through joy, as in Israel's future joyous exodus from exile
subduing one's animality (behemiyut) — 'plowing' the beast-nature ('your field for your cattle'), which reveals the totality of the supernal colors

the revelation of the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob) in the world — the manifestation of the Avot to dispel judgment, darkness, forgetfulness, and foolishness (per Lev. 26:42, 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob'), as expounded in Likutey Moharan I:37
removal of the clouds covering the eye — dispelling the anannin (alien thoughts in prayer) that blind the eye of judgment, restoring Ein Mishpat
yit'aved ra'am — the 'thunder is made' (Zoharic idiom): the purifying thunder produced by the quarrels among true tzaddikim that expels the Other Side

the straightening-out (removal) of the crookedness in your heart — the phrase from Likutey Moharan I:5 (based on Berakhot 59a on thunder), denoting that the heart's twisted, insincere bends are smoothed away so it can rejoice and receive Torah
studying Shas — the counsel (eitza) of learning the Talmud/Gemara (the Oral Torah, comprising the sixty tractates), especially at night, as a rectification

rectifying the six rings (shit izka'in, Zoharic Aramaic) of the windpipe (kaneh/trachea) — the tikkun of the six cartilage rings of the throat from which voice and melody issue, achieved through nightly study of Oral Torah (Gemara), enabling one to hear melody from any person (Likutey Moharan I:3)
Eretz Kena'an — the Land of Canaan expounded as 'ka'an ani' (here is a pauper), the state of poverty caused by machloket (strife)

"here is a poor person" (ka'an ani) — the Talmudic wordplay (Pesachim 50a) reading Canaan/Kena'ani as kan + ani, denoting poverty/loss of livelihood, applied by Rabbi Nachman to the state caused by dispute (Land of Canaan = presence of a pauper)
Kena'an — the name Canaan itself as wordplay 'ka'an ani' (here is a poor man), signifying poverty from dispute (per Pesachim 50a)
Edom — the nation/kingdom of Esau ('who comes from Edom'), identified with the liver (kaved), seat of anger and blood
kaved — the liver, bodily organ of blood and anger corresponding to Edom/Esau, subdued through fasting or Shabbat eating
shultanei rugzin — the Zoharic 'rulers of wrath' (Terumah 135b), wrathful powers embodying the angry liver that flee on Shabbat
kaved ko'es — 'the liver is angry' (physiological dictum): the liver as seat of anger, whose power is nullified by holy Shabbat eating

the crown of kingship (keter malkhut) — the royal crown, drawn from the Talmudic teaching (Yoma 72b with Rashi) that a person's table corresponds to the crown of Malkhut, linked to honor/glory ('the King of glory')
kevod El — 'the glory of God' (Ps. 19:2) as an epithet for prayer ('render glory His praise'), the vessel into which Torah-letters/souls are enclothed

the glory/honor of God (kevod Elokim) — Divine glory as opposed to human or royal honor; the concealed honor belonging to God (per Proverbs 25:2), identified in Likutey Moharan with Malkhut, the 'King of Glory,' which one merits by fleeing personal honor
zevichat ha-yetzer hara — the 'slaughtering' of the evil inclination, accomplished by silence (dom) under insult, God felling its 'corpses'
kavod Eloki — Divine honor/glory (as opposed to one's own honor), attained by staying silent under disgrace and not defending personal honor

canonical_he: על־ידי שמירת הברית בשני הבחינות הנ"ל
gloss_en: shemirat ha-brit in its two aspects — guarding the covenant (sexual purity) in both its higher and lower modes, the means of sustaining 'the glory of God forever'
forms: על־ידי שמירת הברית בשני הבחינות הנ"ל

gloss_en: guarding the covenant (shmirat ha-brit) in both of its two aspects — the Supernal Unification (yichuda ila'ah) and the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah), i.e., Shabbat/weekday union, trees/grasses, Kabbalah/Halakhah — the dual sexual-covenantal purity practice in Likutey Moharan I:11 that brings God's honor to completeness

The perfected/complete state of God's honor (kavod Hashem yitbarakh bi-shleimut) — the condition in which the divine glory attains wholeness, achieved (in LM I:11) through guarding the covenant in both unifications and through utterly distancing oneself from arrogance, which in turn enables the illuminating speech

canonical_he: לפנות את המחין מחכמות חיצוניות וממחשבות זרות
forms: לפנות את המחין מחכמות חיצוניות וממחשבות זרות

canonical_he: מצותא ומריבה שיש בין הצדיקים השלמים
forms: מצותא ומריבה שיש בין הצדיקים השלמים

canonical_he: גבורות בחינת רעמים, צריך לשתף עמהם אהבה
forms: גבורות בחינת רעמים, צריך לשתף עמהם אהבה

gloss_en: striking the glory (kavod) — the aspect of wisdom (chokhmah): the goal that the gevurot/thunders, once joined with love, impact 'glory' (identified with chokhmah per Prov. 3:35) so that thunder is produced (Likutey Moharan I:5)

potential (koach) — the latent, not-yet-actualized state of a thing, paired with and opposed to po'al (the actual/actualized), as in bringing something 'from potential to actual'; the initial thought before the deed

the power/faculty of speech (koach ha-dibbur) — the human capacity for articulate verbal expression, rooted in the mouth and its five articulation points, which distinguishes humans from mute beasts and is drawn from the aspect of the Tzaddik

kelipot — the 'husks' or shells of impurity in Kabbalah: parasitic forces of evil that surround and conceal holiness the way a peel surrounds a fruit, deriving vitality from it while being superfluous to it

the Mishkan — the wilderness Tabernacle (מִשְׁכָּן) erected by Moses, treated in Likutey Moharan I:70 as the aspect of the 'drawing force' (koach ha-moshech) that draws down Godliness, homiletically linked to מָשַׁךְ (to draw) and שָׁכַן (to dwell)

the drawing/attracting force (koach ha-moshech) — the gravitational-like power of earth/dust that pulls things toward itself, which in Likutey Moharan I:70 is the aspect of the humble tzaddik (Moses, dust) and of the Mishkan, drawing down Godliness

the power/force of prayer (koach ha-tefillah) — praying with bodily force so that "all my bones shall say" (Ps. 35:10), the physical energy invested in the words of prayer, corresponding to the 28 letters of the Act of Creation (LM I:48)

"one eyeball" (chad galgala de-eina) — the Zoharic/Idra Aramaic phrase for the single orb of the eye of the Holy Ancient One, identified with the future "one eye of mercy" (eina chad de-rachamei) of undivided compassion, cited in LM 1:4 as the aspect of "kulo haTov vehaMeitiv"

the weaponry of Mashiach (kelei zeino shel Mashiach) — the Messiah's armament, which is essentially prayer (identified with the nose/breath and the guarded covenant), by which he wages all his battles and conquests

the attribute (middah) of Tiferet — the sefirah of harmonizing beauty/splendor identified with Yaakov and truth, which comprises the totality of the colors (kelalut ha-gevanin) and unites fire and water (heavens)

spirit/wind (ruach, Aramaic rucha) — the vital breath or animating spirit-force: the life-breath blown into the nostrils, the wind of the lungs that cools the heart, the spirit residing in the tzaddik ('a man in whom there is spirit'); distinct from revach (profit/space) which shares the letters רוח
wing (kanaf) — the wing/garment-corner as a covering that conceals, linked via Isaiah 30:20 've-lo yikanef od morekha' to the aspects of enclothement (hitlabshut) and the Throne
throne (kisei) — the Divine Throne of Glory (Kisei HaKavod), the seat of God's manifest kingship as in Ezekiel's vision ('above the firmament the likeness of a throne'); not any homograph of כסה/כוס
gevanin ila'in — the 'supernal colors/hues' (Zoharic Aramaic term for the upper sefirotic lights), here identified with silver and gold
kesef ve-zahav — silver and gold as a paired symbol: the physical embodiment of the supernal colors/hues resting on money
ra'ah — 'the evil' unleashed from the north (Jeremiah 1:14), identified as anger (ka'as) descending from the Gevurot, twin of money/gold

anger/wrath (ka'as) — the emotion of rage; in lm1:68 human anger rooted in Gevurot sharing a source with money ("from the north"), and in lm1:18 God's anger (kaʿaso) expressed as concealment of the Divine face
hastarat penei Hashem — the concealment of God's face caused by Israel's lack of faith/heresy, itself an expression of divine anger and wrath
kefirah ba-avodah zarah — the denial/repudiation of idolatry, the trait embodied by Mordecai the 'ish Yehudi' (whoever denies idols is called a Yehudi)

the birds of the kelipah — impure spiritual forces ('birds' dwelling in the husk of impurity) that suckle from the breasts of Malkhut and constitute the mental faculties (mochin) of the Malkhut of the kelipah; the source from which a wicked musician draws his melody (Likutey Moharan I:3, after the Zohar and the Arizal)
the principle 'when it (truth) dwells with you, He will illuminate you' — divine light dwells and shines according to the measure of one's truth, since God is the essence of truth

burnt-offering (olah) — the sacrificial offering wholly consumed on the altar, interpreted in LM I:108 as the aspect of a broken spirit (not the feminine participle 'ascending' עוֹלָה, nor עַוְלָה 'injustice')
hamtakat ha-charon af — the sweetening/mitigation of divine wrath, effected via 'potei'ach et yadekha' whose final letters spell ChaTaKh (= twice ruach), distinguishing right hand from left

canonical_he: כשר ופסול טמא וטהור אסור ומתר
gloss_en: kasher/pasul, tamei/tahor, asur/mutar — the six paired halakhic categories (fit/unfit, impure/pure, forbidden/permitted) comprising the six orders of Mishnah, corresponding to the six weekdays and Metatron
forms: כשר ופסול טמא וטהור אסור ומתר

canonical_he: לסתם את עיניו, ולכון ההסתכלות אל התכלית
gloss_en: the act of shutting one's eyes and aiming one's gaze at the ultimate purpose (tachlit) — contracting physical sight amid suffering so as to focus on the distant final goal
forms: לסתם את עיניו, ולכון ההסתכלות אל התכלית

gloss_en: the practice of binding and elevating speech to its root (Imma/supernal Mother) — 'chariots of Pharaoh' read as tefillin-lights revealed from Imma
learning Torah with another person — the act of teaching a fellow, classed as 'writing' since the tongue engraves words on the student's heart
ketivah — writing as a category of Torah transmission: the tongue as 'the pen of a ready scribe' inscribing teaching on the tablet of the student's heart
the letter kaf — the alphabet letter symbolizing Keter (Crown), the inner soul-dimension linked to the Shekhinah as nefesh
'that which orders and settles the intellect' — the faculty of arranging/composing the mind, identified as Keter (from kattar, 'to wait'), blessed by the inner dimension of the blessings

the upper dot of the letter Alef (the yod-point above the diagonal vav in the letter's form), symbolizing in Likutey Moharan I:6 the concealed supernal throne / Keter, identified with the sun, Moshe, and the higher level of teshuvah
seyag — the 'fence' around wisdom ('a fence for wisdom is silence'), identified as Keter, the encircling crown formed out of silence that surrounds Chokhmah

a person's table (shulchano shel adam) — the rabbinic phrase for one's dining table as a locus of spiritual significance, likened to the altar and to the crown of kingship (cf. Chagigah 27a, Yoma 72b)
shufra di-shufra — 'the beauty of beauty' (Zoharic term): the choicest illumination from the 32 (lamed-bet=lev) Elokim of Creation that nourishes and names the heart
the Mishkan (Tabernacle) in its built state — corresponding to the 39 (lamed-tet/'tal') lights merited by guarding the brit
lamed-tet orot — the thirty-nine ('tal', dew) lights, the illuminations preserved by one who guards the covenant (opposite of the 39 labors/lashes)
the Mishkan (Tabernacle) in its destroyed state — corresponding to the 39 lashes (malkot), the punitive counterpart to the 39 lights (Tikkun 48)
the counterfactual state 'had your brain(-drops) not been blemished' — i.e., if one's seminal/mind drops were intact, referring to pegam ha-brit in the mind

canonical_he: לא היה נשמע לך מריבות שבין הצדיקים
gloss_en: the consequence 'you would not hear the quarrels between the tzaddikim' — hearing tzaddikim's disputes is a rebuke signaling one's own blemished mind-drops
forms: לא היה נשמע לך מריבות שבין הצדיקים

gloss_en: the state of having no distress on the road — safety in travel, contingent on shemirat ha-brit ('all roads are presumed dangerous'; hence visiting one's wife before a journey)

canonical_he: לא יחסר כל טוב, ויהיה כלו טוב
gloss_en: the future messianic state 'no good will be lacking and all will be entirely good' — the era of 'ha-tov ve-ha-meitiv' when increased Da'at brings eternal life
forms: לא יחסר כל טוב, ויהיה כלו טוב

gloss_en: 'lo yitama' — the priestly prohibition against defiling oneself for a corpse (Lev 21), read as guarding the brit from sexual impurity, root of tum'ah
'lo avado' — 'one who does not serve Him' (Malachi 3:18), the type among the four who entered Pardes who ascends beyond his level and is stricken (Ben Azzai's hetzitz ve-nifga)
the alephs in holiness — the holy aleph-letters identified with Leah, which when fallen become the opponents' weariness (hal'ot) and scorn of God-fearers

Leah — the matriarch, wife of Yaakov, understood kabbalistically as the partzuf Leah: the concealed feminine (alma d'itkasya, the hidden world), positioned at the back of the head/neck (oref), the 'first nukva,' associated with the heart and the sweetening of harsh judgments (not the verb לָאָה 'to be weary,' though wordplay with lo'eh occurs)
korban olah — the burnt offering, which is in the aspect of Leah; the daily olat tamid sweetens her judgments against the impure 'worm' of the kelipah

the heart (lev) — the inner organ as the spiritual seat of emotion, intention, memory, and devotion; the inner 'tablet' and hidden chamber of the person (and, cosmically, the supernal Heart), on which Torah is inscribed and from which prayer, joy, and warm speech flow
the Concealed World (alma d'itkasya) — the Zoharic Aramaic term for the hidden, covered supernal world (associated with Leah/Binah), as opposed to alma d'itgalya, the revealed world
the act of swiftly expelling the ruach shetut (spirit of folly) from within oneself — accomplished by binding oneself in soul-love to the true tzaddik
lev nishbar — the broken heart: the heart's contrite state connected with expelling the spirit of folly and being incorporated into the tzaddik's heart

canonical_he: לבוא לאלו הרועים, שהם כלליות של הקדשה
gloss_en: coming/gaining access to the true shepherds (ro'im) who are the collectivity (kelaliyut) of holiness — attainable only through holy boldness (azut, 'bold as a leopard')
forms: לבוא לאלו הרועים, שהם כלליות של הקדשה

gloss_en: hitkarvut la-tzaddikim — drawing close to the tzaddikim and following the path of their counsel, whereby their advice engraves truth (emet) in a person
coming/arriving at truth (emet) — the attainment of truth itself, possible only via closeness to tzaddikim and receiving their counsel (a union/zivug)

canonical_he: תורה שמאירין להם אל מקום שהם שם
gloss_en: the Torah that shines to people in the very place where they are — Torah-light reaching sinners and converts 'chutzah' (outward), via its 600,000 letters matching the 600,000 souls, to awaken teshuvah
forms: תורה שמאירין להם אל מקום שהם שם

gloss_en: hitbodedut — the Breslov practice of secluded personal prayer: setting aside time alone (in a room or field) to pour out one's speech before God in one's own words, in supplication and conversation with the Creator
coming to bittul — attaining self-nullification (nullifying desires, bad traits, and corporeality to be included in one's root), possible only through hitbodedut
attaining mochin zakkim — pure, clarified mental faculties (holiness/purity of thought), the prerequisite for sweetening judgments, sought by traveling to tzaddikim for Rosh HaShanah

garments, clothings (Aramaic plural of levush) — the 'garments' in which spiritual light or the Divine face is clothed/veiled, associated with tzedek (righteousness) as in 'tzedek lavashti' (I clothed myself in righteousness)
nullifying the body entirely — speaking Torah and prayer until the body becomes naught and one flesh with the speech ('ve-hayu le-vasar echad')

canonical_he: מתבודד ומפרש שיחתו בינו לבין קונו
gloss_en: hitbodedut practice — secluding oneself and pouring out one's conversation between oneself and one's Creator, the means to bittul
forms: מתבודד ומפרש שיחתו בינו לבין קונו

gloss_en: the counsel (eitza) of speaking abundantly in words of Torah study and prayer — converting one's blood/vitality into holy speech so as to nullify contentiousness and attain peace (Likutey Moharan I:75)

canonical_he: לבטל מדת הנצחון והמחלקת, ולרדף אחר השלום
gloss_en: nullifying the trait of nitzachon (contentiousness/winning) and machloket (dispute) and pursuing peace — the obligatory eradication of the blood-rooted urge to conquer
forms: לבטל מדת הנצחון והמחלקת, ולרדף אחר השלום

gloss_en: the student/disciple (talmid) — the receiver of teaching from his master (rav), who like the moon receiving the sun's light embodies Lower Wisdom receiving from Upper Wisdom

the Wicked Kingdom (Malkhut ha-Resha'ah) — the demonic counter-Malkhut of the Sitra Achra (the Other Side), the evil parallel to the holy Kingship; identified with the moon of the Other Side, the evil inclination as the 'old foolish king' that rejects wisdom, and the spleen/black bile
levanah de-sitra achra — the 'moon of the Other Side': the demonic counterpart-moon of the wicked kingdom (malkhut ha-resha'ah), of which it says 'the moon will be ashamed' (Isaiah 24)
banim — children/offspring: the merit of begetting sons, attained only through complete da'at (a minor cannot beget, lacking full da'at), as Abraham merited via making converts

the perfection/completeness of speech (shlemut ha-dibbur) — the state in which the letters of holy speech are made whole (via faith and the aspect of the World to Come), exemplified by the 'pure language' of Zephaniah 3:9 when all humanity will call upon God's Name

canonical_he: להחיות את עצמו, ולבוא לידי שמחה
forms: להחיות את עצמו, ולבוא לידי שמחה

gloss_en: bringing the surrounding lights (makifin) inward — causing the transcendent encompassing intellects/lights, which hover outside the inner human intellect and outside the Torah, to enter and be internalized within the inner intellect (in Likutey Moharan I:21, achieved through sanctifying the seven lamps of the face)

canonical_he: ימלא גרונם, על־ידי רקודין, או על־ידי פדיון
forms: ימלא גרונם, על־ידי רקודין, או על־ידי פדיון

canonical_he: להמתיק הדינים, על־ידי שרשם, שהוא יין המשמח
forms: להמתיק הדינים, על־ידי שרשם, שהוא יין המשמח

gloss_en: Torah study at night (limmud ha-Torah ba-laylah) — the devotional practice of learning Torah during the nighttime hours, which draws down a thread of kindness (chut shel chesed) and enables elevating speech to its root

canonical_he: להעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך
forms: להעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך

gloss_en: raising up fallen faith — the act of restoring emunah (specifically faith in the Sages) after it has collapsed, accomplished in Likutey Moharan I:57 through the aspect of Yaakov, i.e., by making and immediately fulfilling a vow

canonical_he: שבח הצדיקים. כשמשבחין ומפארין את הצדיקים
forms: שבח הצדיקים. כשמשבחין ומפארין את הצדיקים

canonical_he: להרועים אי אפשר להתקרב כי אם
forms: להרועים אי אפשר להתקרב כי אם

canonical_he: להרחיב ולהאריך ימיו בתוספות קדשה בכל פעם
forms: להרחיב ולהאריך ימיו בתוספות קדשה בכל פעם

canonical_he: להשלים את דעתו, שיהא שלם בדעת
forms: להשלים את דעתו, שיהא שלם בדעת

canonical_he: רודפים אחר בני אדם לקרבם לעבודתו יתברך.
forms: רודפים אחר בני אדם לקרבם לעבודתו יתברך.

gloss_en: joy of the heart (simchat ha-lev) — inner gladness seated in the heart itself, the heart's rejoicing (as in 'wine gladdens the heart of man'), which requires uprightness of heart and empowers prayer and dance
the left (שְׂמֹאל) — the left side/hand as a kabbalistic aspect (the Gevurah side), associated with Levi, purity, and material bounty ('in her left hand riches and honor'), opposed to the right

melody and joy (niggun ve-simchah) — the spiritual practice of music/song joined with gladness that sifts the good spirit from the evil spirit, thereby guarding memory of the World to Come (Likutey Moharan I:54)
the 'double bread' (lechem mishneh) — the twofold portion of manna/loaves associated with Shabbat (Exodus 16:22), used as a symbol of doubled blessing on Shabbat

the small luminary (ha-ma'or ha-katan) — the lesser light of Genesis 1:16, i.e., the moon that rules the night, serving as the kabbalistic symbol of Malkhut/faith/prayer, the diminished recipient light illuminated by the great luminary (Moses/the tzaddik)

lamdan — a Torah scholar learned in halakhah, specifically one versed in the laws of forbidden and permitted (issur ve-heter), paired with 'tzaddik' as the second requisite of a rabbi and identified with the angel/Metatron aspect (Likutey Moharan I:31)
above time (le-ma'alah me-ha-zeman) — the spiritual state or level that transcends temporality, where time is nullified; attained e.g. through faithful business dealings, thought, or repentance
above nature (le-ma'alah me-ha-teva) — the supernatural realm transcending the natural order, where miracles occur and which prayer accesses by overriding nature's dictates

makifim — the 'encompassing/surrounding lights' (Kabbalistic or makif, plural): transcendent intellect or divine influx too great to enter the brain/inner vessels, which instead surrounds them from outside (e.g., sukkah, chuppah, Atika), as opposed to penimi (inner light)

canonical_he: על־ידי האמירות והדבור של איש הישראלי
forms: על־ידי האמירות והדבור של איש הישראלי

gloss_en: bandits/highway robbers (listim, from Greek lēstēs) — armed brigands who waylay travelers; in Likutey Moharan 4 paired with 'wild beast' (chayah ra'ah) as the danger of the road, representing the evil trait of pride arising from the 'speaking' (human) element

canonical_he: להמשיך קדשת שבת, לקדש ימי החל
forms: להמשיך קדשת שבת, לקדש ימי החל

canonical_he: לקרב את הגרים עם בעלי התשובה
forms: לקרב את הגרים עם בעלי התשובה

canonical_he: שמתיגע בתורה, עד שזוכה לידע אותה ולהבינה
forms: שמתיגע בתורה, עד שזוכה לידע אותה ולהבינה

canonical_he: לרפאות נפשו, דהינו להעלותה למקום שרשה
forms: לרפאות נפשו, דהינו להעלותה למקום שרשה

canonical_he: לתן כח בהם שיוכלו לילך כראוי
forms: לתן כח בהם שיוכלו לילך כראוי

canonical_he: זריזות גדול בעבודתו יתברך, ולרוץ מאד מאד
forms: זריזות גדול בעבודתו יתברך, ולרוץ מאד מאד

canonical_he: מאירין ההתנוצצות האותיות שיש בכל דבר
forms: מאירין ההתנוצצות האותיות שיש בכל דבר

canonical_he: שכשהנשמות עושין פרות שעושין רצונו של מקום
forms: שכשהנשמות עושין פרות שעושין רצונו של מקום

canonical_he: נעשה מכל הדמים, דבורים של תורה ותפלה
forms: נעשה מכל הדמים, דבורים של תורה ותפלה

canonical_he: למסר המלחמה על ה. שה ילחם המלחמה
forms: למסר המלחמה על ה. שה ילחם המלחמה

gloss_en: mevatlim ha-teva — the action of nullifying/overriding nature's determinism through Jewish prayer, countering the philosophers' claim that nature ('mother of all life') is fixed
chai birkhaan — the eighteen (chai=18) blessings of the Amidah prayer (excluding birkat ha-minim), whose recital nullifies nature ('mother of all life') and subdues heretics

seeing the tzaddik — the first of three modes of attachment to the tzaddik (per Isaiah 30:20 'your eyes shall see your Teacher'), whose gaze nullifies bad traits from the mineral/vegetative elements (sadness and evil desires)
gazing upon temunat Hashem — beholding the 'image of God,' i.e. the prophetic anthropomorphic likenesses (Compassionate, Gracious, etc.), attained through clapping palm against palm in prayer

playing an instrument by hand — the musician's hand-motion on the instrument that sifts the good spirit (ruach of prophecy/joy) from the evil melancholy spirit, subduing the imaginative faculty (as David's playing for Saul)
magdilim otah — raising/growing the newborn soul (nefesh) through love (ahavah), the 'great hand' (yad ha-gedolah), following its birth through fear
chut shel chesed — the 'thread of lovingkindness' drawn upon a person (Abrahamic chesed of 'he planted an eshel'), a protective kabbalistic emanation shielding from the serpent
protection from the serpent — the shielding effect of the thread of chesed (Abraham's aspect, the tree in the Maharsha's parable) that guards a person from the serpent of lust/evil
burning heart-heat for God — the fervor of the heart aflame toward Hashem, whose fire-nature expels the spirit of impurity (as fire expels air)
chamimut ha-lev — the heart's heat/fervor as a fire-element force that drives out the impure spirit, analogized to gunpowder's ignition expelling air
speaking more with the Rebbe — the increased personal converse with one's master that flows from holy boldness (azut di-kedushah), the measure of one's closeness to the tzaddik
MaL (מל) — the word 'circumcised' from ChaShMaL (chash-mal), gematria 70, whose cutting nullifies the bonfire of the seventy stars; circumcision as tikkun ha-brit
birthing the mochin — the Shekhinah's 'giving birth' to the withdrawn mentalities: one's cry in prayer/Torah, like a laboring woman's cry, brings the mochin out of their gestational concealment
molid — begetting/procreating, dependent on the letter heh ('hei lakhem zera') and on da'at ('a minor cannot beget'); why Abraham and Sarah bore children only upon receiving the heh
the two hands — yad ha-gedolah (great hand = love, which raises the soul) and yad ha-chazakah (strong hand = fear, which births it), as in 'in Your hand is power and might... to make great'
birthing and raising the soul clothed in Kavod — the twofold action (via fear and love, the two divine hands) of begetting and then growing the nefesh that is garbed in the King of Glory/Malkhut
galgalei ha-rakia — the celestial spheres/star-wheels of the firmament that determine terrestrial conditions (roads, deserts, settlement) and mark time; cause of travelers' sufferings
mo'ed — 'appointed time/festival' in Lamentations 1:4 read as the celestial spheres by which time is reckoned ('roads of Zion mourn without comers to the mo'ed')
charity's efficacy against lustful thoughts — tzedakah as a segulah that protects from hirhurei ni'uf (adulterous fantasies), though one may not rely on it to mingle with women
faith in the tzaddik's words — the believers' emunah in what the tzaddik says, which is itself the agency that causes his latent wonders (moftim) to become revealed
moftim — wonders/miracles of the tzaddikim, revealed publicly (as in the Kaiser's lands) only where the populace has faith in the tzaddik's words

canonical_he: מוצא אני מר ממות את האשה
gloss_en: 'more bitter than death is the woman' — Ecclesiastes 7:26 applied to livelihood earned in sorrow (parnasah = 'woman'), the bitter mode of sustenance needing sweetening
forms: מוצא אני מר ממות את האשה

gloss_en: siftotayikh — 'your lips' (Song of Songs), symbolizing the bringing of the intellect from potential into actuality (mi-ko'ach el ha-po'al) through speech
extracting her from the kelipot — tzedakah's rescue of the soul/Nukva ('her feet go down to death') from among the husks that suck her light and constrict one's sustenance; 'charity saves from death'

canonical_he: מוריד גם־כן חמימות והתלהבות להשם יתברך
gloss_en: movement generating fervor for God — how thought-to-thought motion in contemplating God's greatness 'brings down' heat, setting the heart aflame, like motion melting wax on an arrow
forms: מוריד גם־כן חמימות והתלהבות להשם יתברך

gloss_en: power of prayer-in-awe — the force drawn from tefillah performed with yirah (fear of God, 'my house'), by which the tzaddik rules ('You shall be over my house')

bringing down shefa and magnifying His kingship — the tzaddik's ruling in fear of God draws divine abundance into the world and enlarges God's Malkhut ('by your mouth all my people shall be sustained')
moshel — 'ruler,' the meaning of dabar ('one leader for a generation'); Malkhut as leadership/dominion restored to God via verbal confession before a Torah scholar
atzirut — constipation/retention as the bodily figure of motarot (waste/superfluities); Doeg's Torah study 'detained before Hashem' derived from this excremental aspect, yielding crooked judgment

mizbe'ach be-chelko shel toref — the altar standing in the territory of the 'predator' (Benjamin, per Yaakov's blessing); the completeness of the altar whose flaw empowers idolatry, rectified through converts
'Reprove a wise man and he will love you' (Proverbs 9:8) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the ears (udnin), i.e. hearing the words of the wise
'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord' (Psalms 111:10) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the nose (chotem), the moach manifest in smell/awe
'And the eyes of both were opened' (Genesis 3:7) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the eyes (aynin), the moach manifest in sight
'The beginning of Your word is truth' (Psalms 119:160) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the mouth (peh), the moach manifest in speech
heart's desire revealed in the hands — the cheshek of the heart becoming manifest through the hands ('ki vi' = 42 = 3×yad), i.e. the basis of clapping the palms in prayer
tevel (world) — gematria 432 = 2×216 (right hand 72 subsuming 3×72=216 plus left hand 216), the cosmos-name signifying the union of right and left in hand-clapping
kupah shel sheratzim — the 'basket of vermin hanging behind him' (Yoma 22b): a discrediting blemish required of a communal leader so he not grow arrogant

canonical_he: מחזיק את עצמו בבחינת מה ואפס ואין
gloss_en: self-abnegation of the leader — holding oneself as 'mah,' naught and nothing (ayin), the humility stance that protects the generation's leaders from arrogance
forms: מחזיק את עצמו בבחינת מה ואפס ואין

gloss_en: Shem Yah (יה) — the divine Name Yah, aspect of the mochin (mentalities), by which Scripture testifies to Israel's purity ('tribes of Yah,' the added heh/yud of ha-Chanokhi)
kavanah — the prayer-intention/mental focus aroused by the voice ('the voice arouses the kavanah'), identified with the mochin birthed through crying out
bilbul ha-da'at — confusion of the mind, a mental state identified as mochin d'katnut (constricted consciousness), source of dinim and troubles
shoresh ha-neginah she-bikdushah — the holy root of melody, located in the mochin/da'at of Malkhut of holiness, from which the cantor must draw song
mochin ve-da'at shel Malkhut di-kedushah — the mental faculties and knowledge of the holy Malkhut, the prophetic source-consciousness from which holy melody is drawn
mochin she-be-Malkhut di-kelipah — the mental faculties of the Malkhut of the husks, identified by the Arizal with the impure 'birds' of the kelipah
Sitra Achra — the 'Other Side,' the demonic realm of impurity, here defined as the very aspect of machloket (dispute), rooted in dispute-within-holiness
'ein adam met va-chatzi...' — the rabbinic dictum 'no one dies with half his desires fulfilled,' read as referring to dispute via Targum's 'ba'alei chitzim' = disputants
kol ha-chola'at — all illnesses/diseases, defined as bodily machloket: the four elements warring instead of resting in balanced peace within the body
notzot — feathers (of the geese in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale), symbolizing strife and insults via the wordplay 'ki yinatzu anashim' (Deut. 25)
machloket u-vizyonot — quarrel and humiliations as a paired concept, the strife-and-disgrace symbolized by feathers (notzot/yinatzu)
machloket Shammai [ve-]Hillel — the archetypal dispute-for-the-sake-of-Heaven between the schools of Shammai and Hillel, whose initials spell MoSHeH
machaneh Dan — the camp of the tribe of Dan, the rear-guard 'gatherer of all the camps,' emblem of Malkhut collecting the holy camps
teiku — the Talmudic term for an unresolved halakhic question, read per Zohar (Ra'aya Mehemna) as 'tikkun' missing its final nun, i.e., lacking rectification
mechusar tikkun — the state of 'lacking rectification,' what teiku signifies: tikkun deprived of its nun, an unrepaired deficiency
machashavah techilah — the primal thought preceding action (potential/koach), symbolized by the initial Yud of the Tetragrammaton at the head of the Aleph
Shaddai shel chol — the weekday manifestation of the divine name Shaddai, the contractions between labor and labor, identified with Metatron who rules the six weekdays
'mateh uzkha yishlach mi-Tziyon' — the verse 'the staff of your strength He will send from Zion' (Ps. 110:2), linked to sha'arei/se'arot (gates/hairs) of Zion in the first tikkun of the beard

canonical_he: מי שהוא כשר, נמשכת הנגינה שלו
gloss_en: the principle that a kosher (worthy) person's melody is drawn from the two pure birds of holiness — fitness as prerequisite for untainted neginah
forms: מי שהוא כשר, נמשכת הנגינה שלו

gloss_en: mayin metikin — 'sweet waters,' the taste of sweetness in prayer, identified with pure waters (mayin dakhyan), holy seed, and guarding the brit
MaL — the 'mal' component of ChashMaL, denoting milah/circumcision: cutting away the disgrace-foreskin after the silence (chash)
shalhevet Yah — the 'flame of God' (Song 8:6), a descending holy fire that scorches the three impure kelipot so they cannot grasp holiness on erev Shabbat
mayim chamin — the hot water of pre-Shabbat washing, embodiment of the shalhevet Yah flame that burns off the kelipot on erev Shabbat
mayim karim — cold water that revives the soul, received via thunder generated by honoring an elder who forgot his learning
meimei ha-chesed — the waters of lovingkindness, Avraham's bounty (the well of living water), his attribute of chesed
'meisharim eshpot' — 'I will judge with equity' (Ps. 75:3), taken as the aspect of anavah (humility) in judgment, per Chullin 89
ha-noah veha-anachah — the groan and the sigh, which constitute a quasi-death of both body ('a sigh breaks a person's body') and soul
mitah be-guf va-nefesh — death in body and soul, the twofold dying effected by the groan/sigh (Berakhot 58b; Ps. 104:29)
ra ayin — the evil eye, equated with death of the heart; the cause of forgetfulness that destroys memory ('between your eyes')
the principle that honor rises to its root in proportion to one's rectification of kavod — each honors God-fearers according to how far he has repaired the glory

canonical_he: מכיר ומשיג יותר את השם יתברך
gloss_en: the ever-deepening recognition and apprehension of God — each new level of knowing Hashem that obligates teshuvah upon one's previous teshuvah
forms: מכיר ומשיג יותר את השם יתברך

gloss_en: subduing the 'breath of beauty' (hevel ha-yofi) — the shofar/beard tikkunei Atik action of humbling vain charm, narrow-above-wide-below (min ha-meitzar)
machnia ha-medameh — the subduing of the imaginative faculty (dimyon), achieved by the 'hand' that sorts the good spirit from the evil spirit

canonical_he: מכניע העבודה זרה שנעשה מפגם חלקי המזבח
gloss_en: subduing idolatry that draws its power from the blemished altar-portions — accomplished through converts who complete the pegam ha-mizbe'ach
forms: מכניע העבודה זרה שנעשה מפגם חלקי המזבח

gloss_en: machnia tola dikelipah — the holy worm ('I am a worm, not a man,' the olat tamid/chesed of Avraham) subduing the worm of the kelipah
machni'in oto — subduing him/it (the impure ruach of Esav) via the white tallit and the Thirteen Attributes, the holy ruach-chayim
machni'in ha-ruach se'arah — subduing the storm-wind, the spirit of opponents of true tzaddikim, through the four tzitzit drawing ruach from the four winds (Ezek. 37:9)
'tzaddik moshel' — 'the righteous one rules [over Me]' (II Sam. 23:3), the tzaddik's power over God, present in every Jew ('your people are all tzaddikim')
melo pum — 'full mouth' (Aramaic), the letters of the melupum vowel: the tzaddik's mouth filled with Godliness, aspect of tzaddik-moshel
hitlahavut — fiery enthusiasm/ardor of the heart, an angel-like burning ('angel of God in a flame of fire,' Ex. 3:2) that scorches the chitzonim
malakhim — angels, the fiery beings to which heart-enthusiasm corresponds ('vayera elav malakh Hashem be-labat esh'), whose fire burns the external forces
've-Yosef hu ha-shallit' — the verse 'and Yosef, he was the ruler' (Gen. 42:6), Yosef/Yesod as the melupum-vocalized channel of abundance

king (מֶלֶךְ) — the sovereign ruler as archetype: the appointed monarch of Israel and the tzaddik/Divine King through whom rulership, sustenance, and honor flow; the noun 'king', not the verb מָלַךְ 'to reign', the abstract מַלְכוּת 'kingship', or the idol מֹלֶךְ
Torah scholars (talmidei chakhamim) — sages learned in Torah, 'disciples of the wise,' the rabbinic scholars themselves as persons (not their teachings)

the lower intellect (sekhel ha-tachton) — the contracted, lower level of intellect identified with Malkhut/Chokhmah Tata'ah, the wisdom of governance that garbs and constricts the higher intellect of divine perception, serving as the introduction/gateway to it (Likutey Moharan I:30)

Judah (Yehudah) — the biblical patriarch, son of Jacob, and his tribe/territorial portion; associated in Likutey Moharan with the aspect of Malkhut (kingship) and fear/awe (yirah), and with verbal confession
the kingship/royalty of David (Malkhut David) — the Davidic monarchy as the embodiment of the sefirah of Malkhut, associated with prayer, anointing oil, and song

transgressors (poshe'im) — persons who willfully rebel/sin, the active-participle plural of פ.ש.ע (as in Hosea 14:10 'transgressors stumble in them' and Isaiah 53:12 'numbered with the transgressors'); NOT the abstract noun pesha'im 'transgressions/sins'

standing (amidah) — the verbal noun of עמד, the act/state of standing upright and being firmly established; in Likutey Moharan the symbolic 'standing' that denotes prayer (per 'ein amidah ela tefillah', the Amidah), Torah received while standing, and money/livelihood that stands a person on his feet

canonical_he: ממשיכין אריכות ימים, ואז זוכה לדעת
forms: ממשיכין אריכות ימים, ואז זוכה לדעת

canonical_he: ממשלת וכח הצדיק שנעשה על ידי עבודתו
forms: ממשלת וכח הצדיק שנעשה על ידי עבודתו

canonical_he: מן הנמנע, שלא יבוא לו איזה גדלות
forms: מן הנמנע, שלא יבוא לו איזה גדלות

canonical_he: ירשת ארץ־ישראל, על־ידי המשכת קדשת ארץ־ישראל
forms: ירשת ארץ־ישראל, על־ידי המשכת קדשת ארץ־ישראל

gloss_en: name (the noun shem, שֵׁם) — an appellation/designation, encompassing one's renown or reputation in the world and the Divine Name, homologized in Likutey Moharan with soul/nefesh, vitality, and Malkhut; not the adverb sham (שָׁם, 'there') or the verb sam (שָׂם, 'placed')
Egypt (Mitzrayim) — the biblical land of Israel's bondage and exile, site of the descent of Jacob and his sons and of the Exodus; homiletically linked to constriction (meitzar)

canonical_he: מקבל עליו על מלכות שמים שלמה
forms: מקבל עליו על מלכות שמים שלמה

canonical_he: שמקשר לבו לדעתו, שלבו ברשותו וכו
forms: שמקשר לבו לדעתו, שלבו ברשותו וכו

canonical_he: מקבלין המדות אור האהבה שבדעת וכו
forms: מקבלין המדות אור האהבה שבדעת וכו

gloss_en: the filthy places (mekomot ha-metunafim) — places of filth/excrement, i.e., the lowest, spiritually defiled locations (symbolizing the depths of impurity into which a person may fall), where holiness is concealed

tekhelet — the sky-blue dye/thread of the tzitzit fringes, expounded (via Zohar) as that which 'consumes and destroys all' (linked to kallah/takhlit and judgments/gevurot), symbolizing Malkhut and encompassing lights

divine influx (shefa Eloki) — the divinely bestowed flow of intellect/holy inspiration that comes to a person without preliminary steps, identified in Likutey Moharan 21 with Ruach HaKodesh, the sukkah, the face of the menorah, and the surrounding lights (makifin)

the father's heart becoming circumcised (נִמּוֹל, nif'al 'was circumcised') — the removal of the foreskin/blockage of the parent's heart so it truly feels the pain of his sins, which in LM I:141 awakens the hearts of his descendants (not any other sense of מ-ו-ל or לבב)

canonical_he: לזה עזות דקדשה – הינו קולות הנ"ל
forms: לזה עזות דקדשה – הינו קולות הנ"ל

gloss_en: shepherd (רוֹעֶה) — the spiritual shepherd/leader of the generation, the tzaddik in the aspect of Moses the Faithful Shepherd (רעיא מהימנא) who constructs the Tabernacle from which the children of the generation receive; not a literal herder of flocks, nor רֵעֶה (friend) or רָעָה (evil)

Torah scholar (talmid chakham) — the sage learned in Torah who, in Likutey Moharan 4, embodies the aspect of Moses: the true scholar before whom one makes verbal confession, who is bound to the light of Torah, and who guides each person on the path according to the root of his soul

blemish of the covenant (pegam ha-brit) — the spiritual damage caused by sexual sin, i.e. violation of the covenant of circumcision through wasted seed or sexual immorality, the counterpart of shemirat ha-brit
restoring the soul (meshivat nafesh) — the phrase from Psalms 19:8 'the Torah of God is perfect, restoring the soul,' denoting the Torah's power to revive and return the nefesh to its root
diminishing and belittling oneself — the practice of self-effacing humility (making oneself small/few, like dust), which draws the Divine presence (per Chullin 89a on Deut. 7:7)

completing/filling the deficiency (mashlim ha-chisaron) — the remedying of a lack in any matter by drawing the spirit of life (ruach chayim) back to it, e.g., through sighing or Torah and prayer, since every deficiency is essentially a departure of that thing's vital spirit (Likutey Moharan I:8)

the Mishnah — the corpus of Oral Torah (six orders of tannaitic teaching) that delineates legal opposites (pure/impure, forbidden/permitted, valid/invalid), identified in the Zohar/Tikkunim with the angel Metatron and the six weekdays; not מִשְׁנֶה 'double/copy/viceroy'

square (ribbua) — the quadrate/squared figure, paired with the circle (iggula) in LM 59 as the aspect of judgment (mishpat), associated with 'hand'; the geometric-kabbalistic square, not any other sense of the root רבע

the first-person pronoun "I" (ani, אֲנִי) — the scriptural word for selfhood/divine self-reference, expounded as the aspect of Malkhut/judgment (e.g. "va-ani natati lekha", "va-ani betokh ha-golah"); not אֳנִי (a fleet of ships) or עָנִי (a pauper)

canonical_he: מתחלה היצר הרע מתלבש עצמו במצוות
forms: מתחלה היצר הרע מתלבש עצמו במצוות

canonical_he: מתמלל ומשתבר אש המדורה של שבעין כוכבין
gloss_en: the breaking-down and nullification through speech (mitmalel u-mishtaber) of the bonfire-fire of the seventy stars — i.e., the Holy Tongue's power to 'speak down' and shatter the fire of the seventy nations' languages/celestial powers (the 'mal' of Chashmal, in Likutey Moharan I:19)
forms: מתמלל ומשתבר אש המדורה של שבעין כוכבין

canonical_he: התנוצצות האור שמקבל הלב מל"ב אלקים
forms: התנוצצות האור שמקבל הלב מל"ב אלקים

forms: מתפללין כסדר התפלה, ואין צריך להלביש התפלה

gloss_en: hearing the melody/music (listening to the נְגִינָה played by a worthy musician, which in Likutey Moharan I:3 rectifies the aspect of malkhut)

canonical_he: מתרבה הרחמנות והשלום. ועל כן הפרנסה בנקל
forms: מתרבה הרחמנות והשלום. ועל כן הפרנסה בנקל

canonical_he: נאכל להצדיק ונתהפך למהות הצדיק ממש
forms: נאכל להצדיק ונתהפך למהות הצדיק ממש

canonical_he: נאספו החרפות, הינו השלש קלפות כנ"ל
gloss_en: the 'gathering in' (removal/nullification) of the disgraces (charafot) that beset a person — identified with the three impure kelipot associated with the foreskin — accomplished through circumcision/guarding the covenant (as in 'God has gathered in my disgrace' at Joseph's birth and 'today I have rolled away the disgrace of Israel')
forms: נאספו החרפות, הינו השלש קלפות כנ"ל

canonical_he: נבנה ירושלים, קריה נאמנה, הינו שזוכין לאמונה
forms: נבנה ירושלים, קריה נאמנה, הינו שזוכין לאמונה

gloss_en: Nogah (kelipat Nogah) — the fourth, translucent 'glowing' husk of the kabbalistic kelipot (from Ezekiel 1:4, 'a radiance surrounding it'); the intermediate shell mixing good and evil that, unlike the three wholly impure husks, can be clarified and absorbed into holiness — locus of free choice and trial, linked to Chashmal, Targum, and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Not the planet Venus, not generic 'brightness,' and not the verb נָגַהּ 'to shine.'

canonical_he: ברור הרוח טובה מן הרוח רעה
forms: ברור הרוח טובה מן הרוח רעה

gloss_en: melody/tune (niggun) — musical melody as a spiritual act that gathers and clarifies the good spirit from the evil/animal spirit; not the verb 'to play' nor the player

"We will do" (na'aseh) — Israel's declaration at Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 24:7, "na'aseh ve-nishma"), signifying the revealed commandments one knows how to fulfill, as opposed to nishma (the hidden); not the passive verb "is made/done"

the revealed things (niglot) — the openly revealed dimension of Torah and its commandments, which each person knows and is able to fulfill according to his level; paired opposite of nistarot (hidden things), and identified in LM I:22 with 'we will do' (naaseh)

"his Torah" (torato) — the Torah that becomes the person's own possession (per Avodah Zarah 19a on Psalms 1:2: first 'the Torah of God,' then 'his Torah'); the internalized, revealed level of Torah corresponding to na'aseh ('we will do') and 'the revealed things belong to us,' in contrast to torat Hashem, the hidden nishma level

canonical_he: התגלות ההתפארות שמתפארין ישראל עמו יתברך
forms: התגלות ההתפארות שמתפארין ישראל עמו יתברך

gloss_en: the engraving of an evil letter-combination (tzeruf ra) upon a person's bones as the imprint of his transgression (per Ezekiel 32:27, 'their iniquities were engraved upon their bones'), whereby each sin inscribes its destructive letter-permutation into his very skeleton

canonical_he: נחקק ונרשם מקום בלב המתבקש לקבל הבקשה
forms: נחקק ונרשם מקום בלב המתבקש לקבל הבקשה

gloss_en: one's thought becomes purified — the cleansing of a person's mind/thought (נִטְהָר, nif'al of ט-ה-ר, 'is purified' + מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ 'his thought'), the spiritual outcome (in LM I:234, effected by telling stories of tzaddikim) whereby mental confusion and impure thinking are removed

canonical_he: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם
forms: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם

forms: שישראל עושין רצונו של מקום, ונכללין בשרשם

forms: נכלל כל העולם שנברא בשבילם, בחיוב המציאות

canonical_he: נכללים שמאל בימין, וימין בשמאל ונעשים אחדות.
forms: נכללים שמאל בימין, וימין בשמאל ונעשים אחדות.

canonical_he: לשפך שיחו בתפלה לפני השם יתברך
forms: לשפך שיחו בתפלה לפני השם יתברך

canonical_he: נכנסין כל הנדחין מקדשת ישראל לתוך הקדשה
forms: נכנסין כל הנדחין מקדשת ישראל לתוך הקדשה

gloss_en: the spiritual outcome whereby foolishness (kesilut, the kelipot's folly) is subdued and the intellect (sekhel) is elevated/magnified — the effect achieved through eating with kashrut (LM I:17)

canonical_he: מזבח כתקונו, הינו שהאכילה בכשרות כראוי
forms: מזבח כתקונו, הינו שהאכילה בכשרות כראוי

canonical_he: לעין בתורה, עד שמשיג חכמות התורה
forms: לעין בתורה, עד שמשיג חכמות התורה

gloss_en: the subduing of the character traits and desires of the idolatrous nations — the evil middot and lusts rooted in the darkened faces (anpin chashukhin), which are subjugated when one attains the Torah's wisdom (illuminated faces)

"a grease-stain found on his garments" (Talmudic phrase, cf. Shabbat 114a, רְבָב on a scholar's clothes) — used in LM 29 as the emblem of soiled garments signifying the blemish of the covenant (pgam ha-brit)

the drawing of wealth into length of days — the process (in Likutey Moharan I:60) whereby material riches (עשירות) are channeled into and contained within the aspect of longevity/length of days (אריכות ימים, the elder/Atik rectifications), so that wealth becomes bound to extended life rather than standing alone

miracles (nissim, plural of nes) — supernatural events above and contrary to the course of nature, wrought through prayer and faith and centered in the Land of Israel; not נָסִים 'fleeing' (participle of נו״ס) nor נֵס as mere 'banner/pole'

"the Torah of the LORD" (torat HaShem) — in R. Nachman's reading of Avodah Zarah 19a on Psalms 1:2, the Torah as it belongs to God before one has labored in it: the hidden, not-yet-attained dimension of Torah (bechinat nistar, 'the hidden things belong to God'), corresponding to nishma ('we will hear'), as opposed to torato, 'his own Torah,' the revealed/naaseh portion

Sha"Kh (שַׁ"ךְ) — the kabbalistic number 320, the 320 judgments (Shach dinim): five times din (דין = 64, ×5 = 320), equal in gematria to na'ar (נער, 'lad'), associated with the bride/Malkhut as the aspect of concentrated judgments
dances / dancing (rikkudin) — the joyful bodily act of dancing, especially at weddings and in worship, by which the feet are elevated and judgments sweetened

the residual trace (reshimu) of the unity of Ein Sof that remains imprinted in a person after returning from ecstatic cleaving (devekut), preserving the knowledge of that unity in his restored conscious mind

entering the 'returning' (va-shov) phase — the ebb of 'running and returning' (ratzo va-shov) in which, after ecstatic self-nullification and cleaving to the Ein Sof, one returns to embodied existence and conscious mind (da'at) so that his being is sustained

canonical_he: שמעורר בני אדם משנתם על־ידי ספורי מעשיות
forms: שמעורר בני אדם משנתם על־ידי ספורי מעשיות

gloss_en: the fulfillment of one's petition — 'his request is done/actualized' (naʿaseh baqashato): the granting of a prayer-request, brought from potential into actuality (through speech/Torah shaping the letters for good); not 'we will do' (naʿaseh of Sinai) nor a request merely uttered

canonical_he: מש הגוף להנשמה בעשית מצוו‍ת מעשיות
forms: מש הגוף להנשמה בעשית מצוו‍ת מעשיות

canonical_he: העלאת מיין נוקבין של תורה ותפלה
gloss_en: the elevation of mayin nukvin (feminine waters) effected by the words of Torah study and prayer — the arousal from below through sacred speech that unites and makes peace above (Likutey Moharan I:75)
forms: העלאת מיין נוקבין של תורה ותפלה

gloss_en: the forging of a combination (tzeruf) from the fallen sparks (nitzotzot) whereby a world is made — cosmogonic act of birur/rectification underlying strife's transformation

the creation of a new heaven and new earth — cosmic renewal effected by praising God with strength from eating the true abundance that flows via the Land of Israel (per Zohar intro 5a, 'imi — My partner')
the letters becoming shaped/configured (nitztayru ha-otiyot) — imprinting a form for good on the letters of speech so one's request is actualized

canonical_he: נעשים כלי לקבל טוב, ונתמלא בקשתו בפעל
gloss_en: becoming a vessel to receive good so one's request is filled in actuality — the state effected when will (desire) plus speech bring the soul from potential to act
forms: נעשים כלי לקבל טוב, ונתמלא בקשתו בפעל

gloss_en: the ongoing action of searching out and gathering additional good points (nekudot tovot) within oneself despite their admixture with dross (Azamra practice, LM I:282)
melodies (niggunim) being formed from the gathered good points — music arising from collecting the good spirit out of the depressed spirit (cf. LM I:54, playing on an instrument)
ha-kissufin ve-ha-cheshek — holy yearning and desire to perform a mitzvah, the affective force that draws vowel points (nekudot) to the letters (wordplay: kissufin/kesef of 'nekudot ha-kasef')
vowel points (nekudot) being formed — creation of the letters' vocalization through holy yearning (kissufin), per Song 1:11 'nekudot ha-kasef'
've-atzi'ah She'ol hinekha' (Ps. 139:8, 'if I bed in the abyss, You are there') — proof-verse for expertise in 'returning' (baki be-shov), the descent phase of teshuvah (aspect of ve-nafik, exiting)
've-dodi li' ('and my Beloved is mine,' Song 6:3) — mapped to ve-nafik/exiting, the 'expert in returning' pole of the run-and-return dynamic of teshuvah

canonical_he: נפסק מחבל דטמאה, ונתקשר בחבל דקדשה
gloss_en: being severed from the rope of impurity and bound to the rope of holiness — the transfer of attachment effected through the sigh/groan (hevel of the mouth) of the penitent
forms: נפסק מחבל דטמאה, ונתקשר בחבל דקדשה

gloss_en: gan — 'garden' as symbol of the nefesh (soul), per Jer. 31:12 'their soul shall be like a watered garden,' the Gan of Gan Eden paired with Eden=ultimate purpose

Ruth (the Moabite, biblical ancestress of David, book of Ruth) — the personal name רוּת, expounded via Berakhot 7b ('from her came David who saturated [riva] God with songs and praises') as a symbol of the soul/prayer

yearnings/longings (kisufin) — the soul's intense desires and cravings for something (esp. longing for God), which Rabbi Nachman teaches form the nefesh, punned with 'nekudot ha-kasef' (Song 1:11); not 'silver' (kesef) itself
vowel points (nekudot) — the Hebrew vocalization marks that animate and combine the letters, serving as the letters' soul/vitality (as opposed to dots in general, drops, or the verb 'to punctuate')
'chasidekha' ('Your pious ones,' Ps. 145:10) — exegeted as the aspect of nefesh/soul, via Prov. 11:17 'a man of chesed benefits his own soul'
the throne (kisse) on the level of nefesh — the 'concealed' (mekhusseh) soul-throne in the soul/ofanim/throne schema, i.e., the hidden precious soul of the sage
nefesh he-chakham she-nitkasseh — the concealed soul of the wise man, hidden because of its preciousness (Prov. 3:15 'more precious than pearls,' cf. High Priest entering the innermost sanctum)
the totality of her (the wife's/lower level's) nefesh-ruach-neshamah — the complete soul-complement of the feminine/lower rung, which counts as mere 'nefesh' relative to the man above it
'nefesh relative to him' — the relational status whereby an entire lower level (even with all three soul-parts) ranks as nefesh/feminine vis-à-vis the level above it
'yehalekhun' ('they walk,' from the verse) — exegeted as the souls (nefashot), via the wordplay mehalakh (walking/movement) = nefesh, souls that progress
the opening of the gates of holiness — messianic result when the gate of the Sitra Achra (gate of Aram) falls its third time and Ben David builds the gates of kedushah
'ruach apeinu...' ('the breath of our nostrils,' Lam. 4:20) — proof-phrase for the two ruchot (spirits/breaths) encoded in ChaTaKh = twice 'ruach' (gematria of the acrostic of 'pote'ach et yadekha')

canonical_he: נפתחין ונחתכין הידים, שהם בחינת שתי הרוחות
gloss_en: the hands being opened and 'cut'/distinguished (nifta chin ve-nechtakhin) — the differentiation of right from left hand as the two ruchot, encoded in the acrostic ChaTaKh of Ps. 145:16
forms: נפתחין ונחתכין הידים, שהם בחינת שתי הרוחות

gloss_en: melamdin alav zekhut — Heaven's advocacy/pleading of merit on behalf of the tzaddik in judgment (Berakhot 7b, 'he prevails in judgment'), the mechanism shielding him from the wicked's evil eye

canonical_he: נצול הצדיק מרע עין של הרשע
gloss_en: the tzaddik being saved from the evil eye (ra ayin) of the wicked — deliverance effected by God's own merit-finding for the rasha, removing judgment from the tzaddik
forms: נצול הצדיק מרע עין של הרשע

canonical_he: מה שהוא בעצמו שופט את עצמו
gloss_en: self-judgment (mishpat) — the practice of a person judging and adjudicating himself over every deed before acting, the 'king through mishpat' that establishes fear/eretz
forms: מה שהוא בעצמו שופט את עצמו

gloss_en: being spared from the heavenly judgment (din shel ma'alah) — the exemption gained when one judges oneself below, so the court above need not judge him
the perfection of da'at as the internalization of makkifim — transcendent surrounding lights (makkifim) becoming inner lights (penimiyim), completing the mind
being saved from all troubles (nitzol mi-kol tzarot) — the protected state attained through perfected da'at, likened to escaping an ambusher by changing garments/face
being saved from all of them (the three ambushers: wild beast, bandits, crossroads dangers) — deliverance via the three practices culminating in verbal confession before the talmid chakham
tzedakah given to a Torah scholar — the specific charity-act that saves from the evil traits of the 'animal' and 'speaking' elements (wild beast = idle talk, bandits = pride)
being saved from foreign thoughts (machshavot zarot) that confuse prayer ('the flood/mabbul') — protection gained by giving charity for the Land of Israel and being included in it
being saved from adultery (ni'uf) and meriting shemirat ha-brit — sexual purity attained through humility (anavah), since arrogance leads to stumbling with a married woman (Sotah 4b)
being saved from transgressions (averot) through giving tzedakah — compassion from Heaven grants da'at, and with da'at no 'spirit of folly' can lead one to sin

being saved from the 'face of the Sitra Achra' — protection from the Other Side's countenance attained through tikkun ha-brit (rectified sexual covenant), which also rectifies niddah-blood/money-craving
being saved from troubles (tzarot) by telling stories of tzaddikim — since confusion of mind is mochin de-katnut (constricted consciousness = judgments), and tzaddik-stories bring expanded mochin
the act of giving ma'aser (the tithe) — the tenth-giving that invokes God's sheltering hand ('in the shadow of My hand I covered you') against enemies
being saved from enemies/haters (son'im) — the divine protection of the pursued ('God seeks the nirdaf') secured through giving the tithe

being saved/rescued from destitution and poverty (nitzolin mi-dalut va-aniyut) — deliverance from material impoverishment, attained in LM I:47 through breaking the craving for food, via the truth-aspect of Yaakov and tefillin
being saved from mikreh lailah (nocturnal seminal emission) — nocturnal purity achieved via perfection of the Holy Tongue (leshon ha-kodesh) with Targum, as with Elisha ('a holy man')
'lekhet' ('to walk,' from Micah 6:8 'hatznea lekhet') — exegeted as the sefirot Netzach and Hod (the two legs/full sukkah walls), paired with hatznea = Yesod
Netzach and Hod — the paired seventh and eighth sefirot (Eternity/Victory and Splendor) in Kabbalah, corresponding to the two legs/feet, associated with prophecy, walking, and Torah scholars
the simple supernal light becoming configured (nitztayer) according to the receiving vessel — the tzeirei-vocalization principle that the undifferentiated light takes the shape of its kli
the totality of the lower rung (klal ha-madregah ha-tachtonah) — the principle that any entire lower level is 'nefesh'/feminine relative to the rung above it
the feminine (nekevah) — the female principle in Kabbalah, the receptive lower aspect (identified with nefesh, the wife, the feet) relative to the masculine level above it

canonical_he: בימי רבן גמליאל היה הדור, שהיתה תורתם
forms: בימי רבן גמליאל היה הדור, שהיתה תורתם

canonical_he: נתבטל הדאגה של החטא המונעת השמחה
forms: נתבטל הדאגה של החטא המונעת השמחה

canonical_he: נתבטל רצונו מפני רצון השם יתברך
forms: נתבטל רצונו מפני רצון השם יתברך

canonical_he: נתבטלין ונכנעין אלופי עשו, רברבי עשו
forms: נתבטלין ונכנעין אלופי עשו, רברבי עשו

canonical_he: מתפלל בכל כחו ומכניס כחו באותיות התפלה
forms: מתפלל בכל כחו ומכניס כחו באותיות התפלה

canonical_he: נתקרבו, בחינת: "ועמדו רגליו על הר הזיתים"
forms: נתקרבו, בחינת: "ועמדו רגליו על הר הזיתים"

canonical_he: תורה, שעל ידה נתעורר מדת אברהם
forms: תורה, שעל ידה נתעורר מדת אברהם

canonical_he: סתירת הפתח, שהוא המדמה, שהוא הטמאה
gloss_en: setirat ha-petach — demolishing the doorway (from the elders-of-Athens riddle): the counsel of tearing down the medameh/imagination, identified with impurity, so one can enter the gate of holy intellect
forms: סתירת הפתח, שהוא המדמה, שהוא הטמאה

gloss_en: Ayin-Bet Resh-Yod-Vav (72 + 216) — gematria pair of divine names (Chesed 72 / Gevurah 216) whose sum equals ibur (288, 'grain/pregnancy') in the Rabbi Yonah rain story
yare'ach — the moon as celestial body/symbol, called 'servant' (sihara) in the Zohar, ruling over the four elements beneath its sphere
the evil character traits (middot ra'ot) deriving from the four physical elements, termed 'servants' because the elements lie beneath the lunar sphere — nullified in 'out of the house of bondage'
kefirot — heresies/denials of God, defined as an aspect of idolatry (avodah zarah)
shemirat ha-mo'ed — the act of guarding/honoring the festivals, whose neglect equals idol worship (Rashi on the juxtaposition of idolatry and festivals)
avodah tamah — 'complete/unblemished divine service,' the Temple-service term applied to festival observance as the opposite of idolatry
shishim (sixty) — the number sixty as the measure of nullification of forbidden food (bittul be-shishim), symbolizing the circle (igula), the letter samekh, the Throne of Glory, and 'sixty queens'
the practice of speaking words of Torah and prayer until the body is nullified — speech-devotion uniting body with holy speech ('they shall be one flesh')
the state of bodily self-nullification (bittul) attained through Torah and prayer speech — the body becoming null and naught, one with the word
boshet — shame/bashfulness as a spiritual quality, root of holy boldness, identified with Eden ('the shame-faced goes to the Garden of Eden')
the or ha-ganuz — the hidden primordial light stored away for the righteous in the future, the 49 lights, 'Eden which no eye has seen'
the 'od sheli' — the 'yet/more' one finds within oneself (from 'azamrah l'Elokai be-odi'), the residual good point enabling one to sing to God
the verse 'od me'at ve-ein rasha' (Ps 37:10) — 'yet a little and the wicked is no more,' judging oneself favorably by the small good point that renders one no longer wicked
zivchei Elohim — 'the sacrifices of God' (Ps 51:19), interpreted as the olah burnt-offering equated with a broken spirit (ruach nishbarah)
olah (ascent) of the two Houses — 'Mi with Zot ascends': the rising together of Binah (upper house, 'Mi') and Malkhut (lower house, 'Zot')
the ascent/rectification of speech (dibbur, called 'foot/regel') via Shabbat — 'if you restrain your foot on Shabbat,' repairing speech damaged by the serpent's contamination
the agency of 'these lights' (the aforementioned orot) — through which one ascends to delight in Shabbat, riding 'the high places of the earth' (Avraham and Yitzchak, the arms of the world)
the state of ascending and delighting in oneg Shabbat — Shabbat-delight attained via the lights and the patriarchs ('az titanag al Hashem')

canonical_he: עולים כל הניצוצות על־ידי אחד־עשר סממני הקטרת
gloss_en: the elevation of all fallen sparks via the eleven spices of the ketoret (incense) — raising sparks from among the idolaters through faithful commerce ('yod'ei teru'ah' as joining)
forms: עולים כל הניצוצות על־ידי אחד־עשר סממני הקטרת

gloss_en: the divine name combination El-Havayah (E-l + YHVH) — signifying alma de-atei, the World to Come, drawn into this world
dibbur shel Shabbat — the speech of Shabbat ('ve-daber davar'), the World-to-Come speech that must be drawn into and complete weekday speech
olam-shanah-nefesh — the Sefer Yetzirah triad World/Year/Soul, the three statures (komot) that receive vitality from the mitzvot
osek be-dinei mamonot — engagement in monetary law/judgments, equated with the plain sense of Torah and honest commerce (the 'sleep' aspect of Rosh Hashanah)
the act of speaking with the Rebbe/master — the disciple's boldness-enabled conversation with his teacher, the measure of closeness to him
the state of doing and laboring much in divine service — abundant active worship, itself dependent on holy boldness (azut dikdushah)
histaklut be-vitachon — the gaze of trust: looking with one's eyes to God alone in bitachon ('the eyes of all look to You'), which fashions a vessel of boundary and time for the divine flow
the making of wings of holiness (kanfei dikdushah) — forming the six holy wings/handbreadths of the brit (circumcision-covenant), as in the six-winged seraphim
the act of taking speech from da'at (knowledge/awareness) — drawing the word from the mind so it contains the good that makes it heard and accepted
the act of putting the good into speech — infusing dibbur with tov so that it is heard and accepted ('the good — all desire it')
the transformative act of making tzedek into tzedakah — adding the heh of five chasadim via charity, elevating fallen Malkhut from 'her feet descend to death'
iza — the 'goat' of Rav Ashi's sea-goat (Bavli aggadah), read as oz (might/strength), i.e., fear of God, 'the glory of their strength'
azut de-sitra achra — brazenness of the Other Side, the profane bodily impudence (azut ha-guf) opposed to holy boldness

canonical_he: עבודתו שהוא עושה ועובד הרבה את ה
gloss_en: one's own divine service ('that he does and labors much for God') — the personal avodah about which one must boldly speak with the Rebbe
forms: עבודתו שהוא עושה ועובד הרבה את ה

gloss_en: azut le-daber im ha-rav — the specific boldness to speak freely with one's Rebbe/teacher about all one's needs without shame, the measure of closeness
the verse 'im esak shamayim sham atah' (Ps 139:8) — 'if I ascend to heaven, You are there,' signifying ayil (entering), expertise in ratzo (running upward) in teshuvah
the phrase 'Ani le-dodi' (Song 6:3) — 'I am my beloved's,' read as the aspect of ayil (entering/ascending), the baki be-ratzo of repentance
eina chad de-rachamei — the Idra's 'one eye of mercy' of the future time (the single eyeball), the all-good Ein Sof gaze of 'wholly good and beneficent'
ir Elokeinu — 'the city of our God' (Ps 48), the aspect of 'house' to which prayer is elevated from mountain and field, revealing God's kingship to the nations
the phrase 'ir ve-kadish min shemaya nachit' (Daniel 4:10) — 'a wakeful holy one descended from heaven,' whose acronym spells Shimon, alluding to the tanna Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai

canonical_he: שיודע בדעת ברור שהכל בהשגחה מהשם יתברך
forms: שיודע בדעת ברור שהכל בהשגחה מהשם יתברך

gloss_en: the Tree of Life (Etz HaChaim) — the paradisal tree of Genesis 2:9 as a kabbalistic symbol of unblemished divine vitality and the Torah itself, contrasted with the Tree of Knowledge/Tree of Death
willows of the brook (arvei nachal) — the willow branches of the Four Species (Lev. 23:40), homiletically linked via the wordplay arvin/arvei to the feet as 'guarantors' and to channels of water

herbs / grasses — plural of עֵשֶׂב, the plants/vegetation of the field (which grow by rain under their appointed stars and serve as the source of medicinal remedies, and symbolically correspond to souls)
wealth (ashirut) — material riches/prosperity as a spiritual attainment, granted through fear of Heaven and truth
charon af — 'fierce anger'/burning wrath, the divine (and human) attribute of anger that must be sweetened, imaged as smoke rising from the nostrils (Ps. 18:9)
the smoke issuing from His nostrils (Ps. 18:9 'smoke went up in His nose') — the bodily/anthropomorphic image of charon af, divine burning anger
asarah minei zimrah — the ten kinds of song/melody, corresponding to the ten expressions of Psalms, whose power nullifies the kelipah (basis of the Tikkun HaKlali's ten psalms)

canonical_he: עשרה לשונות שנאמר בהם ספר תהלים
gloss_en: the ten expressions (leshonot) with which the Book of Psalms was composed — Ashrei, Lamnatzeach, Maskil, Halleluyah, etc. (Pesachim 117a; Zohar)
forms: עשרה לשונות שנאמר בהם ספר תהלים

gloss_en: asarah minei nigguna — the ten types of melody symbolized by the letter Yud (numerical value 10) within the Hei, linked to the future song (simple-double-triple-quadruple)
ishah ra'ah — the 'evil woman/wife,' a kelipah-figure identified with the 'evil time' (et ra'ah), counterpart to the evil maidservant opposing the Shekhinah

the "evil time" (et ra'ah) — the time/hour of evil, a designation for the domain of the Sitra Achra (identified with the evil woman and the evil maidservant, Malkhut of the Other Side) that rules when holiness is blemished
shifchah bisha — the 'evil maidservant' (Aramaic), the kelipah that usurps the Shekhinah/Malkhut, identified with the 'evil time' (et ra'ah)
sippurei ma'asiyot shel shanim kadmoniyot — telling stories/tales of ancient years, an activity that is the aspect of Atik (the most ancient partzuf), signified by the carob/elder

"abundant in kindness" (rav chesed) — the Divine attribute from Exodus 34:6 ("abundant in kindness and truth"), invoked here as equal in gematria to Mordekhai (274) and identified with the supernal aspect of Atik
'the one seated upon the throne' — the enthroned figure of the Chariot vision identified as Atik Yomin (Daniel 7:9 'and the Ancient of Days sat')
Atik Yomin — the 'Ancient of Days' (Dan. 7:9), the highest partzuf of Keter, here the one who sits upon the throne above the four chayot
shefer — 'beauty/fine' (from 'imrei shafer,' Gen. 49:21), wordplay-cognate of pe'er (glory), the aspect of tefillin and the illumination of Jacob's face
