watering the garden — the act (מַשְׁקֶה אֶת הַגָּן) by which the voice/melody, likened to the river issuing from Eden (Gen 2:10), irrigates the supernal garden where fragrances and awe/fear grow (Likutey Moharan II:8)
fragrances that grow in the garden — holy scents (symbolized by mountains and hills) nurtured in the supernal garden
harim u-geva'ot — 'mountains and hills' of Song 2:8, symbol of fragrances over which the future song leaps
the Ten Utterances (asarah ma'amarot) — the ten divine sayings of Genesis 1 through which the world was created and is sustained, the 'tools' of the work of Creation
the revelation of the Divine glory (kavod) — the disclosure of God's honor effected through the 'staff of strength' (the true leader's power), which in turn enables prophecy (Likutey Moharan II:8)

the 'staff of strength' (mateh oz, Psalms 110:2) — the forceful, judgment-charged prayer of the spiritually mighty person (baal koach), which lodges in the throat of the Sitra Achra forcing it to disgorge the swallowed holiness of Da'at, subdues Amalek, and reveals the Divine glory (Likutey Moharan II:8); מַטֵּה = staff (not מִטָּה, bed)

the prayer of the ba'al koach (person of great spiritual power, e.g. Pinchas) — a prayer deliberately offered in the aspect of constriction/judgment (din) that lodges in the Sitra Achra's throat and forces it to disgorge the swallowed prayers (Likutey Moharan II:8)

constriction and judgment (kimmutz va-din) — the contracted, severity-laden quality characterizing the prayer of the ba'al koach, likened to the 'staff of strength' and wordplay on kumtza (ant/handful) in LM II:8

canonical_he: שהסטרא אחרא שיש לה יניקה מן הדעת
gloss_en: the Sitra Achra insofar as it draws nurture (yenikah) from holy Da'at — the demonic parasitism on the knowledge of holiness, exemplified by Og
forms: שהסטרא אחרא שיש לה יניקה מן הדעת

gloss_en: Og king of Bashan — the giant whose grip is in the 'right side,' sucking from holy Da'at, who uprooted the three-parasang mountain against Israel
the three kinds of compassion (shloshah minei rachmanut) drawn from the three mochin (intellects), which correspond to the three daily prayers, in Likutey Moharan II:8

the three daily prayer services (Shacharit, Minchah, Maariv) — the fixed thrice-daily prayers, which in Likutey Moharan II:8 are drawn from the three mochin and correspond to the three kinds of compassion
mechitzot perusot — 'spread-out partitions,' the wordplay on 'parsei' (parasangs): the three brain-membranes/partitions guarding the camp's holiness
'tura' — the mountain of the Og aggadah (Berakhot 54b), interpreted as prayer, per 'My holy mountain... My house of prayer' (Isa 56:7)

canonical_he: בחינות תלתא פרסי, הינו תלת מחין
gloss_en: 'telata parsei' (three parasangs) as the telat mochin — the three brains/mental faculties from which prayer and the camp's guarding derive
forms: בחינות תלתא פרסי, הינו תלת מחין

gloss_en: guarding against the lust of adultery — the sexual self-guarding that constitutes the holiness of the camp of Israel
shemirah from ta'avat ni'uf via the three mochin — protection from sexual lust (nocturnal emission) effected by the three brains
garon — the throat, the bodily organ emerging from the lung, seat of 'honor God mi-geronekha' (from your throat)
the imaginings/fantasies that come upon a person during sleep — dream-images generated by the cold-moist imaginative faculty
the rainy season — the cold-damp time when sleep falls upon a person, physiological trigger of sleep and imagination
the falling of sleep upon a person — the state of drowsiness induced by cold and moisture (as in rainy weather)
sleep-and-imagination as a paired phenomenon — both dependent on the cold-moist lung, the physiological root of dreaming
the essential sustaining (kiyum) of da'at/intellect — maintained through the body's fat delivered by the lung's breathing
shamnunit ha-guf — the fat/oiliness of the body, the fuel on which the intellect burns like a candle-flame
the essence of the brain and da'at as dependent on bodily fat raised to the brain by the lung's respiration
the sustaining of all the body's fat through breathing — respiration preserving the intellect's oily fuel
the essence of da'at and the mochin (mentalities) — rooted physiologically in the body's fat, hence perfected via the lung
the lung's function of cooling the body's heat — tempering bodily fire, part of its wholesome constitution
tzinah u-kerirut — chill and coldness, the cold-moist quality of the lung underlying sleep and imagination
extracting all the swallowed holiness from the Sitra Achra — the mighty one's din-prayer (like Pinchas) that reclaims captured kedushah

the nullification/abolition of false beliefs (bitul emunot kozviyot) — the breaking down of idolatrous, deceitful faiths, associated in Likutey Moharan II:8 with the shevarim shofar-blast ('you shall surely break their monuments') and paired with the rectification of holy faith
hashra'at ha-Shekhinah — the indwelling of the Divine Presence, signified by 'teruah of the King' (Targum: 'the Shekhinah of their King is among them')
the moment of extraction from the Sitra Achra of what it swallowed — when even its own life-essence is drawn out with it

canonical_he: מוציאין גם עצמות חיותו, שהוא בחינת גרים
gloss_en: drawing out the Sitra Achra's very life-vitality along with the swallowed holiness — this essence being the aspect of gerim (converts)
forms: מוציאין גם עצמות חיותו, שהוא בחינת גרים

gloss_en: the state in which da'at (holy knowledge/awareness) and the brain/mind are restored to wholeness and perfection — attained when the swallowed holiness of da'at is recovered from the sitra achra; identified with Rosh Hashanah as rectification of the head and mind (LM II:8)
the Sitra Achra's returning of the swallowed holiness of Da'at — whereupon the mind/Da'at becomes whole (Rosh Hashanah, tikkun of the 'head')

prayer in the aspect of judgment (din) and justice (mishpat) — the Rosh Hashanah mode of prayer that, as 'the judgment belongs to God,' forcibly extracts the life-force and sustenance the Sitra Achra drew from Israel's Da'at and prayers (LM II:8)
mismus — the 'melting/crushing' wordplay on 'mas oved' (Gen 49:15): Issachar's tribute-service read as the dissolution linked to bearing prophecy's yoke
ha-niggun, bechinat shir chadash — the melody as aspect of the 'new song' (shir chadash) of the future redemption, the song of wonders/providence
nittaken ha-rei'ach — the rectification of the sense of smell, the faculty restored through prophecy/rebuke (scent of the souls)
the "new song" (shir chadash) — the eschatological song of the future, associated in Likutey Moharan II:8 with melody/niggun and the renewal of the world, to be awakened in the time to come
the making of converts (gerim) and the consequent revelation of God's glory (kavod) — the paired effect wrought by prayer in Likutey Moharan II:8, which in turn causes prophecy to spread
nifla'ot shelo ke-derekh ha-teva — wonders/miracles beyond the natural order, i.e., conduct by pure Divine providence rather than nature
yitnaheg ha-olam al yedei nifla'ot — the future state in which the world will be conducted solely through wondrous providence after the renewal of the world
lehitkarev le-manhig amiti — the act of drawing close/attaching oneself to a true leader (tzaddik), sought through searching and prayer
she-yizkeh le-emunah amitit bi-shleimut — the goal of meriting true, complete holy faith (emunah), attained via closeness to the true leader
she-zokheh lehitkarev la-manhig ha-amiti — the merit/state of being drawn close to the true leader, whereby one's imagination and faith are rectified
nittaken ve-nitbarer etzlo bechinat ha-medammeh — the rectification and clarification of the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medammeh) effected in the follower by the leader's prophetic spirit
ha-ruach ha-kodesh she-yesh le-ha-manhig ha-amiti — the true leader's measure of holy spirit (ruach ha-kodesh), his 'different spirit' that is an aspect of prophecy

canonical_he: נתחזק ונתתקן אצלם האמונה האמתית דקדשה
gloss_en: nitchazek ve-nittaken etzlam ha-emunah ha-amitit di-kedushah — the strengthening and rectification of true holy faith in those who draw near the true leader
forms: נתחזק ונתתקן אצלם האמונה האמתית דקדשה

gloss_en: nittaken ha-medammeh — the rectified state of the imaginative faculty, achieved when it is 'in the hand of the prophets' (Hosea 12:11)

canonical_he: שנתקבצין ונתרבין ביותר נפשות ישראל ביחד
gloss_en: she-nitkabtzin ve-nitrabin beyoter nafshot Yisrael be-yachad — the gathering/aggregation of many Jewish souls together (kibbutz of Israel), which magnifies prayer
forms: שנתקבצין ונתרבין ביותר נפשות ישראל ביחד

canonical_he: נתרבה ונתגדל ביותר מאד מאד בית התפלה
gloss_en: nitrabeh ve-nitgadel beit ha-tefillah — the exceeding enlargement of the 'house of prayer,' prayer magnified by each added Jewish soul/neighbor
forms: נתרבה ונתגדל ביותר מאד מאד בית התפלה

gloss_en: u-khe-she-nislach he-avon — the state following forgiveness of sin, when the darkening cloud is removed and the sun shines to heal
selichat he-avon — forgiveness of sin, effected by abundance of prayers that disperses the sin-cloud so the healing sun shines

canonical_he: העננים, שהם הסטרא אחרא והקלפות, כלים והולכים
gloss_en: ha-ananim, ha-Sitra Achra ve-ha-kelipot kalim ve-holkhim — the dissipation of the 'clouds' (the Other Side and husks) through prayer, allowing the glory to be revealed
forms: העננים, שהם הסטרא אחרא והקלפות, כלים והולכים

gloss_en: zerichat ha-shemesh — the shining/rising of the sun as symbol of the revelation of God's glory that brings healing (Malachi 3:20)

rectifying and subduing the war of Amalek — the tikkun that repairs and vanquishes Amalek's spiritual assault, i.e. the defilement of sexual lust (nocturnal emission) that Amalek draws from the blemished Da'at, accomplished through the aspect of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds (Likutey Moharan II:8)

canonical_he: התפלה של הבעל כח בחינת פינחס
gloss_en: ha-tefillah shel ha-ba'al koach, bechinat Pinchas — the forceful judgment-prayer of the man of spiritual power (aspect of Pinchas), the 'staff of strength' lodged in the Sitra Achra's throat
forms: התפלה של הבעל כח בחינת פינחס

gloss_en: shibbarta rashei taninim al ha-mayim (Ps 74:13) — the breaking of the sea-serpents' heads, i.e., subduing the swallowing Sitra Achra to force it to disgorge holiness
nikhna bechinat ekev de-Sitra Achra — the subjugation of the 'heel' of the Other Side, its lowest grasp humbled through the rectifying voice
gedelim sham kol ha-reichot — the garden (watered by the voice/river from Eden) as place where all holy fragrances and fears grow
ke-she-ha-mokhiach ra'ui lehokhiach — the qualified rebuker: one fit to give rebuke, whose reproof adds fragrance to souls rather than fouling their scent
mosif ve-noten rei'ach tov be-ha-neshamot — the effect of worthy rebuke (like Moshe's after the Calf) that adds a good scent to the souls ('my nard gave forth its fragrance')
klei melakhah shel ma'aseh bereishit — the 'tools' of the work of Creation (symbolized by the ten-cubit axe, narga), instruments of the world's fashioning
mezona de-nishmata — Zoharic term: the 'food of the soul,' the sustenance of the neshamah (fragrance/spiritual nourishment) as opposed to bodily food

canonical_he: בטול אמונות כזביות ותקון האמונה הקדושה
gloss_en: bittul emunot kozviyot ve-tikkun ha-emunah ha-kedoshah — the nullification of false beliefs and rectification of holy faith, effected via the shofar sounds/rectified imagination
forms: בטול אמונות כזביות ותקון האמונה הקדושה

canonical_he: כשרואה אדם שבוער ביותר חוץ מהמדה
gloss_en: ke-she-ro'eh adam she-bo'er beyoter chutz me-ha-middah — the state of seeing oneself burning with fervor beyond proper measure, the storm-wind over-inflaming the heart (harisah, 'breaking through')
forms: כשרואה אדם שבוער ביותר חוץ מהמדה

gloss_en: ve-chozer u-vo'er la-Shem yitbarakh — the heart's renewed, regulated burning toward God after the lung-wind cools its excess fire
afruriyut — earthiness/dusty sluggishness, the coarse element that dampens the heart's fervor (source of melancholy)
marah shechorah — black bile/melancholy, the depressive humor that clouds the mind and prevents guiding the brain at will
liba de-khol alma — Aramaic: the 'heart of the whole world,' the tzaddik/leader who functions as the cosmic heart
liba — Aramaic 'the heart,' the bodily organ of the Tikkunei Zohar passage that would burn the whole body without the lung-wings' breeze
manhigei ha-dor — the leaders of the generation, who correspond to the lung-wings cooling the world's heart
bedichah da'atah — cheerfulness/merriment of mind (Talmudic term), the joyous mental state enabling settled awareness
lema'lah na'aseh mi-zeh yichud gadol — the great supernal unification (yichud) effected Above by one's joy in his good point/Jewishness

the liberated mind (ha-moach meshuchrar) — the state in which the brain/intellect is freed and unfettered, achieved by binding joy to one's mind, enabling settled awareness (yishuv ha-da'at); from Likutey Moharan II:10
yishuv ha-da'at — settled mind/composure of thought, the deliberate mental clarity whose lack keeps people far from God
she-mekasher ha-simchah le-mocho ve-da'ato — the act of binding joy to one's brain and awareness, so that the mind can be governed at will
she-motzeh be-atzmo eizeh nekudah tovah — finding in oneself some good point (nekudah tovah, per 'azamerah' Torah 282) as the path to joy

one's mind and awareness becoming free (ben chorin) — the state, attained through joy (the world of freedom, 'for with joy you shall go out'), in which the mind and da'at are liberated from the exile imposed by melancholy, enabling one to direct the mind at will and settle one's thoughts (Likutey Moharan II:10)

canonical_he: יוכל להנהיג את מחו כרצונו ולישב דעתו
gloss_en: yukhal lehanhig et mocho kirtzono u-leyashev da'ato — the capacity, given by joy (world of freedom), to direct one's brain at will and settle one's mind
forms: יוכל להנהיג את מחו כרצונו ולישב דעתו

gloss_en: ke-she-mekasher simchah el ha-mo'ach — the condition of joining joy to the brain, the prerequisite state for attaining yishuv ha-da'at

canonical_he: נעשין בן חורין ויוצאין מן הגלות
forms: נעשין בן חורין ויוצאין מן הגלות

gloss_en: the ability to direct/steer one's mind (moach) at will — mastery over one's own thought processes, which is possible only through joy and impossible under melancholy (Likutey Moharan II:10)

secharchar — 'going round and round' (Psalms 38:11, 'libi secharchar,' my heart reels); the dizzying encircling of the heart by confused thoughts, which R. Nachman links via the Aramaic 'sechor sechor' (around) to kelipat Nogah that surrounds ('ve-nogah lo saviv') and twists the heart

canonical_he: קדם שמחדשין יש כמה ספקות ובלבולים
forms: קדם שמחדשין יש כמה ספקות ובלבולים

canonical_he: הוא חוזר ועולה אל הכבוד העליון
forms: הוא חוזר ועולה אל הכבוד העליון

canonical_he: נצול הצדיק האמת מפגם הצדקה שלהם
forms: נצול הצדיק האמת מפגם הצדקה שלהם

canonical_he: התחברות שמתחברין האמרי שפר עם המלך
forms: התחברות שמתחברין האמרי שפר עם המלך

canonical_he: שכל הפרנסה של ישראל צריכין לקבל
forms: שכל הפרנסה של ישראל צריכין לקבל

gloss_en: elevating the fallen fears — the spiritual practice/process of raising degraded, misdirected awe (fear mixed with foolishness, e.g. fears of worldly things) back to their root, restoring them as complete fear of Heaven joined with Da'at (as taught in Likutey Moharan II:17)
yere Shabbat — one who fears Shabbat: fear of God attained in the Shabbat state, contrasted with weekday fear mixed with foolishness (LM on Shabbat-yirah with Da'at)
ta'anug ve-simchah shel Shabbat — the delight and joy of Shabbat as a devotional state, source of complete fear-with-Da'at, opposed to weekday servitude

freedom (cherut) as the absence of servitude (shi'bud) and exile (galut) — the liberated state characteristic of Shabbat, in which the mind (da'at) is unconfused and complete, unlike the weekday state of bondage that muddles awareness (LM II:17)
yirah bi-shleimut im Da'at — fear of God in completeness, i.e. fear joined with mature awareness (Da'at), free of the foolishness of Job 4:6

Amalek (עֲמָלֵק) — the biblical nation/archetype of heresy, here specifically as the spiritual force of philosophical denial and godless intellect: the 'stumbling stone' of heretical wisdom that denies faith and fear of God
ha-pilosofim ve-ha-kofrim — the philosophers and heretics as a class of persons who allegorize the whole Torah and its practical mitzvot into mere 'form and intellect'
even negef be-khol chokhmah — the 'stumbling stone' lurking within each of the seven secular wisdoms, identified as the aspect of Amalek that causes the inquirer to fall into heresy

the essential/primary attainment of the ultimate purpose (ikkar hasagat ha-takhlit) — the true means of reaching life's final goal, achieved through simple faith and practical mitzvot rather than philosophical inquiry
mitat ha-ishah ha-harah — the death of the struck pregnant woman (Ex 21:22 'ason'), symbolizing destruction of the hidden path/wisdom itself as punishment-scenario, not mere miscarriage
ha-derekh chokhmah be-atzmo — the 'way of wisdom' itself (Prov 4:11), the new spiritual path in gestation, which strife may ruin along with its premature offspring
ishah harah — the pregnant woman of Ex 21:22 as symbol of a spiritual path still in gestation/concealment before its revelation to the world
ha-mefursamim she-na'asin kodem zemanam — leaders who become famous before their time, spiritual 'stillbirths' (nefalim) expelled prematurely by strife, punished with death or poverty
yotze kodem zemano — emerging before one's time: premature exit from the hidden gestation (ibbur) of a new path, producing a nefel-like figure
beginning to enter a path — the initial entry into a not-yet-revealed spiritual way, constituting the state of herayon (conception/pregnancy) requiring concealment
herayon — pregnancy as kabbalistic symbol: the gestation-stage of a new spiritual path/teaching still concealed (linked to Prov 4:11 'be-derekh chokhmah horeitikha')

canonical_he: ללמד פוסקים קדם החדוש שמחדש ואחר כך
gloss_en: studying poskim (halakhic codes) before and after innovating chiddushei Torah — the protective practice surrounding Torah novellae
forms: ללמד פוסקים קדם החדוש שמחדש ואחר כך

canonical_he: נעשין בחינת אנשי חיל מלפניהם ומלאחריהם
gloss_en: anshei chayil formed before and behind — the guard of 'men of valor' (cf. Song 3:7-8) generated by poskim-study, stationed around Torah novellae so no stranger (zar) approaches
forms: נעשין בחינת אנשי חיל מלפניהם ומלאחריהם

gloss_en: when a person is joyful — the state of simchah in which melancholy and sufferings are pushed aside to the periphery (setting of the dance-circle parable)

canonical_he: המרה שחרה ויסורים נסתלקים מן הצד
gloss_en: the melancholy (marah shechorah) and sufferings withdrawing to the side — the displaced-but-not-transformed sorrow standing outside the circle of joy
forms: המרה שחרה ויסורים נסתלקים מן הצד

gloss_en: simchah ve-ha-rikkudin — the joy and dancing (the machol/dance-circle) that heals and into which even the bystander-sorrow is forcibly drawn; foretaste of the future dance
cholah/machol — the dance-circle of the righteous in the World to Come, at whose head God will stand (Yerushalmi Sukkah wordplay rosh cholah)
tikkun ha-cholah — rectification via the dance-circle (machol), the future perfected joy that heals illness (choleh) born of melancholy
making Torah into prayer — the practice of turning learned Torah into personal supplication during hitbodedut, which generates great delight above
sha'ashu'im gedolim le-ma'alah — the great supernal delight aroused Above by hitbodedut speech and turning Torah into prayer
attaining great stature — the high spiritual level reached by every soul, small or great, through the practice of hitbodedut
the 248 limbs (ramach evarim) — the body's limbs corresponding to the 248 positive mitzvot, each clothed with Moshe who reminds it of its mitzvah
hitlabshut Moshe ba-evarim — Moshe Rabbeinu's enclothement within every limb of each Jew, prompting each limb to its mitzvah (forgotten through drunkenness)
hitlabshut ha-Da'at ba-chasadim — the kabbalistic enclothement of Da'at within the chasadim (kindnesses), the structure affected by measured drinking
mitpateh u-mitpayes — being appeased and conciliated: the softening/sweetening effect on judgments when Da'at is elevated through proper measured drink
when the Da'at is elevated — the state of uplifted awareness/mind (via moderate drink) that raises the chasadim clothed within it
the chasadim being elevated and magnified — the growth of the kindnesses that accompanies the broadening and elevation of Da'at
drinking in measure according to one's capacity — moderate wine-drinking suited to one's level, which broadens Da'at rather than causing drunkenness
one's mind broadened and brain elevated — the cognitive expansion (harchavat ha-da'at) produced by properly measured drinking
a little drinking according to need — the small, necessary quantity of drink that benefits and broadens the mind (vs. excess)
leharchiv da'ato — broadening one's Da'at/mind: expansion of consciousness as the beneficial effect of minimal drink
meriting the annulment of vows (hatarat nedarim) — attaining release from one's vows, whose delay otherwise causes idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, and evil speech (Likutey Moharan II:27)
being saved from the four traits — deliverance from idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, and evil speech (the four evils of the delayed vow, per Vayikra Rabbah on Jacob)
assessing each person fairly — the just leader's practice of weighing each individual to apportion the communal burden rightly, which nullifies the four evil traits

canonical_he: יכול להכיר את איש ישראלי בין האמות
gloss_en: the ability to recognize a Jew among the nations — the discernment power (parallel to distinguishing which Torah may be written) to identify an ish Yisraeli among the gentiles
forms: יכול להכיר את איש ישראלי בין האמות

gloss_en: ha-yichudim ve-ha-zivvugim — the supernal unifications and couplings (of divine partzufim), all of which are the aspect of 'nullifying the forbidden' (bittul issur)
bittul issur — halakhic nullification of a forbidden admixture in the permitted, serving as symbol of supernal unification (forbidden becoming permitted, as arusah→nesuah)

The destruction and uprooting of the books of the heretics (sifrei ha-minin) — the on-high kal vachomer outcome in Likutey Moharan II:32 whereby, since even God's holy Name/holy books may be erased for the sake of peace, the heresy-spreading books that cast hatred and strife among Israel are all the more surely blotted out and eradicated
the loss of holy books — the burning/perishing of tzaddikim's sacred writings, likened to the Sotah scroll's divine Name erased for marital peace

canonical_he: שבשביל השלום שביניהן נמחין ונאבדין הספרים
gloss_en: books erased and lost for the sake of peace between them — the sacrifice of holy writings ('My Name written in holiness') to preserve the peace of the supernal holy couple
forms: שבשביל השלום שביניהן נמחין ונאבדין הספרים

gloss_en: when the books are burned and lost — the tzaddikim's deliberate concealment/destruction of their Torah writings to remove the ruach kin'ah (spirit of jealousy) threatening the holy couple's union

canonical_he: הצדיקים הגדולים להעלים תורתם, לשרפן ולהאבידן
gloss_en: the great tzaddikim's concealing of their Torah by burning and destroying it — a deliberate act to remove the spirit of jealousy and protect the peace of the holy couple
forms: הצדיקים הגדולים להעלים תורתם, לשרפן ולהאבידן

gloss_en: godel ha-ahavah — the greatness/intensity of love, the cause on account of which the spirit of jealousy arises even among the pure
the act of being jealous over her — the spirit of jealousy's zealous guarding of the beloved (the holy couple), an expression of true love per the Zohar
ruach kin'ah — the 'spirit of jealousy' (Numbers 5:14), identified as the spirit of Mashiach that is zealous against adultery

The 'spirit of God' (ruach Elokim) — the divine spirit that hovered over the waters (Genesis 1:2) and filled Bezalel with wisdom (Exodus 31:3); in Likutey Moharan the God-given prophetic/inspired spirit identified with the spirit of Mashiach, the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) of the true leader (Moshe), and the mochin — not 'wind' in the meteorological sense, nor a human spirit as such
bechinat Mashiach — the 'aspect of Mashiach,' a messianic quality/level present within a person or a tzaddik's Torah-book
'according to his holiness and purity' — the measure of a person's sanctity and purity that determines the degree of the aspect of Mashiach he possesses
the state of possessing an aspect of Mashiach — having a share of the messianic spirit by virtue of one's holiness

canonical_he: שמי שנכתב בקדשה, ונתפשט בעולם ועושה שם
gloss_en: 'My Name that was written in holiness' (sotah-scroll phrase) — the divine Name inscribed in sanctity that spreads through the world and makes a name, identified with the holy book (sefer = shem by gematria)
forms: שמי שנכתב בקדשה, ונתפשט בעולם ועושה שם

gloss_en: the Name of God (Shem Hashem, שֵׁם ה') — the divine Name of the Tetragrammaton as a sacred entity/presence, e.g. 'a strong tower is the Name of God' (Prov. 18:10), identified with the holy book (sefer = shem in gematria) and with the tefillin/pe'er ('the Name of God is called upon you')
hitnotzetzut — the sparkling/flashing of light that flashes from one joy to its fellow when joys are included together
the growing and increase of the light — the intensification of joy's radiance produced by joys being merged at their root
kelaliyut — the inclusiveness whereby one joy is incorporated into its fellow, the mechanism that magnifies joy's light
the maximal magnification of the light of the joys — the greatly increased radiance resulting from all joys being included together at their single root
coming to mochin de-gadlut — the transition to expanded consciousness (kabbalistic 'mentalities of greatness'), identified as hamtakah (sweetening of judgments)
seeing the tzaddik in his beauty and splendor — beholding the true tzaddik at the time of the gathering (kibbutz), the fulfillment of 'the king in his beauty shall your eyes behold' (Isaiah 33:17)
merchakim — 'far distances' (Isaiah 33:17 'eretz merchakim'), a name for chokhmah/wisdom perceived from afar, linked to the Land of Israel

truthfully gazing upon the true tzaddik — attentively beholding the genuine tzaddik (who, by drawing people to God's service, embodies God's glorying in Israel), the practice by which one comes to 'see' the divine self-glorification and receive its glory/mochin (LM II:40)
receiving from the hitpa'arut — obtaining pe'er (glory) and mochin from beholding God's glorying in Israel, which forms tefillin within the beholder
bechinat einayim — the 'aspect of eyes': spiritual eyes formed when the tefillin-mochin break through, becoming like the eyes of Hashem that watch over the Land
hitpa'arut — God's glorying/taking pride (in Israel), the divine self-adornment from which the tefillin-pe'er and divine 'eyes' of providence are formed

canonical_he: נשמות ישראל, שהשם יתברך מתפאר בהם
gloss_en: the souls of Israel as the object of God's glory — nishmot Yisrael in whom God takes pride ('Israel in whom I glory,' Isaiah 49:3), the source arousing divine providence
forms: נשמות ישראל, שהשם יתברך מתפאר בהם

gloss_en: hitpatchut ha-chokhmah — the opening/unfolding of wisdom, the intellectual expansion produced by the air of the Land of Israel that makes wise

canonical_he: שהשם יתברך מסתכל בארץ ישראל תמיד
gloss_en: God's constant gazing at the Land of Israel — perpetual divine providence over Eretz Yisrael ('the eyes of Hashem are upon it from year's beginning to year's end')
forms: שהשם יתברך מסתכל בארץ ישראל תמיד

gloss_en: the sanctity of the Land of Israel and its wisdom-conferring air — Eretz Yisrael's property of sanctifying and its atmosphere that 'makes wise' (avira de-Eretz Yisrael machkim)
speaking faith aloud with the mouth — the verbal articulation of emunah, which itself constitutes faith and brings one to faith ('I will make known Your faithfulness with my mouth,' Ps 89)
ha-nekudah ha-penimit — the inner point: Shabbat as the central point from which the six weekdays (the surrounding circles) draw sustenance; symbol of the true tzaddik one travels to
the obstacles, incitements, and enticements — the kelipah-generated hindrances that block one from reaching the tzaddik, mere illusions like the Baal Shem Tov's imaginary walls
chomot — the illusory walls of the Baal Shem Tov's parable, conjured by the king around his treasure; obstacles that are only achizat einayim (optical illusion)
speaking of the salvation of Israel — discourse about yeshu'at Yisrael, the holy speech near which the subtle kelipah lurks at the giving-over of Torah
the fleeing of the subtle kelipah — the escape/dispersal of the fine husk that borders holiness when it is denied nurture during the tzaddik's Torah teaching

canonical_he: ולעשות עניני שטות וצחוק או קפיצות ורקודים
gloss_en: doing acts of silliness, laughter, jumping and dancing — deliberate foolish merriment used as a device to attain and maintain joy
forms: ולעשות עניני שטות וצחוק או קפיצות ורקודים

gloss_en: 'and then it will depart' — the withdrawal of the disturbing thought/evil inclination when one stubbornly refuses to attend to it
the evil inclination's departure — the yetzer hara giving up and going away when a person is firm-minded and obstinate against it

canonical_he: אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך
forms: אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך

gloss_en: the fittingness of there being unanswerable questions upon God — kushiyot on the Blessed One as proper and beautiful given His exaltedness beyond our minds

canonical_he: מעצם גדלתו ורוממותו, שהוא מרומם מאד מדעתנו
gloss_en: God's immense greatness and exaltedness beyond our understanding — the very transcendence that makes it necessarily impossible for our minds to grasp Him, hence the questions
forms: מעצם גדלתו ורוממותו, שהוא מרומם מאד מדעתנו

gloss_en: revealing chasadim — the disclosure of divine kindnesses effected through revealing novel Torah insights (chiddushei Torah)

canonical_he: שמה שנמשך אלקותו יתברך, כביכול, ברהטי מחין
gloss_en: the flowing of God's divinity, as it were, into the 'runnels of the brains' (rehatei mochin) — Godliness drawn down into the channels of the mind through Torah innovation
forms: שמה שנמשך אלקותו יתברך, כביכול, ברהטי מחין

gloss_en: tefisah — the prison/imprisonment: Rabbi Akiva's incarceration, attributed by Rabbi Shimon to his expounding Torah publicly before unworthy hearers
the drawing down of Elokut — divinity being drawn into the world through revealed Torah innovations ('that they take for Me an offering')
kesil — the 'fool': the unworthy hearer of Torah (also the star-name Kesil/Orion), into whom honor is diverted when unfit students listen
talmid she-eino hagun — an unworthy/unfit student whose hearing of publicly taught Torah causes withholding of rain
chiluf ha-kavod — the exchange/diversion of honor: glory passing from the Torah to the unworthy, disrupting the cloud-and-rain flow that depends on kevod HaShem

canonical_he: נותן כח בעשבים, ויש מרעה לבהמות
forms: נותן כח בעשבים, ויש מרעה לבהמות

gloss_en: the three colors of the eye together with the pupil (bat ayin) — the Zoharic/kabbalistic aspect of the eye's components (tlat gevanin de-eina u-vat ayin), drawn from the four-letter Divine Name and corresponding to the mochin, the power of sight, and the letters of Shabbat (shin = three colors, bat = pupil), as expounded in Likutey Moharan II:67
the beauty and splendor (yofi u-pe'er) of the world — the epithet in Likutey Moharan II:67 for the true tzaddik (identified with Yosef) as the world's aesthetic glory and adornment

"Rosh Bayit" (Head of the House) — Rabbi Nachman's homiletic reading of "Bereishit" (בראשית = ראש בית) in Likutey Moharan II:67, denoting the true tzaddik as the head/master of the house of the world, from whom all generations are drawn and through whom the Temple and the dwellings of Israel are sustained

the Master of the House of the world (baal ha-bayit shel ha-olam) — the true tzaddik as the world's householder/proprietor, the 'head of the house' (rosh bayit = Bereishit) from whom all generations are drawn and through whom the Temple and Israel's dwellings are sustained (LM II:67)
the true tzaddik (הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת) — the singular authentic righteous leader of the generation, the Yosef-figure who is the beauty and splendor of the world and its 'master of the house'

the power/faculty of sight (koach ha-re'ut) — the visual capacity of the eye, which in LM II:67 is drawn from the divine Name (the four letters), the source of the three colors of the eye and the pupil
the famous men of falsehood (mefursamim shel sheker) — leaders with false, undeserved renown who oppose the true tzaddik and draw their status from the side of impurity

the light/luminary of the eyes (me'or ha-einayim) — the illuminating power of eyesight, identified in Likutey Moharan II:67 with the 'luminaries of light' (me'orei or) and with the three colors of the eye plus the pupil, all drawn from the Name of God

dwelling (dirah) — a residence/abode, specifically the dwelling-place of the Divine Presence below, as embodied in the Holy Temple (and illuminated by Shabbat); not any verbal or other homographic form

mourning (hitpael, mit'abel) — actively grieving over the destruction of the Holy Temple / Zion, the mourning that subdues the luminaries of fire and strengthens the luminaries of light (Likutey Moharan II:67)

canonical_he: מכניע מאורי אש, ומתגברין מאורי אור
forms: מכניע מאורי אש, ומתגברין מאורי אור

canonical_he: כשנתגלה הפאר והיפי של הצדיק האמת
forms: כשנתגלה הפאר והיפי של הצדיק האמת

canonical_he: יכול לראות ולהסתכל בגדלת השם ולהסתכל בעולם
forms: יכול לראות ולהסתכל בגדלת השם ולהסתכל בעולם

canonical_he: תקונם של אלו המחין של חוץ לארץ
forms: תקונם של אלו המחין של חוץ לארץ

gloss_en: inheritance/heritage (נַחֲלַת, construct of נַחֲלָה) — the hereditary portion or estate, as in 'nachalat Yaakov' (the boundless heritage of Jacob, Isaiah 58:14) and 'nachalat' of Psalms 16:6, linked in LM II:71 to tzedakah and the flow of the Supernal Pleasantness

beautiful of form (yefeh to'ar) — the biblical epithet of physical comeliness/handsome appearance (as said of Joseph, Gen. 39:6), used in LM II:71 as an aspect of beauty (linked to Shifrah, 'making beautiful') connected to the revelation of honor and the Supernal Pleasantness

"who are pleasant [to one another] in halakhic discussion" (she-man'imim ba-halakhah) — the Talmudic description (cf. Sanhedrin 24a) of Torah scholars of the Land of Israel who treat each other graciously in halakhic debate, linked here to no'am (Supernal Pleasantness) as the aspect of the rectified 'mentalities of the Land of Israel,' in contrast to the 'destroyers' (chovlim) of outside the Land

pleasantness (noʿam) — the Supernal Pleasantness (nōʿam ha-ʿelyon), the sweet delightful divine flow associated with the mentalities of the Land of Israel; not the proper name Naʿam or naʿim as adjective

terumah — the dedicated offering/heave-offering (as in the Tabernacle donation, 'you shall take My terumah'), which Rabbi Nachman identifies with charity given from generosity of heart, forming a vessel to receive the Supernal Pleasantness (its letters being the final letters of 'lachazot be-no'am H' u-levaker be-heikhalo')

greatness (gedulah) — the noun for exalted stature, eminence, and majesty that a person receives (identified with the sefirah Malkhut and, at its core, with humility); not the feminine adjective gedolah ('large/great')

canonical_he: מקבל כל אחד גדלה כפי מדרגת מחו
forms: מקבל כל אחד גדלה כפי מדרגת מחו

gloss_en: the sparking/illumination of one's mind (mitnotzetz mocho) — the flash of mental enlightenment kindled in a person's individual intellect when the comprehensive sage (chakham ha-dor) gazes upon him, which is the channel through which he receives greatness (LM II:72)

chiddushin de-Oraita — original novel Torah insights/novellae (Aramaic: 'novelties of the Torah'), the new interpretations and elucidations of Torah that the tzaddik-leader of the aspect of Moshe attains through the sparkling of his mind

canonical_he: חוזר ונחיה השפלות של כל אחד
forms: חוזר ונחיה השפלות של כל אחד

canonical_he: מחיב שירגיש כל אחד שפלותו באמת
forms: מחיב שירגיש כל אחד שפלותו באמת

canonical_he: שבא אצל צדיק אמתי ושומע מפיו תורה
forms: שבא אצל צדיק אמתי ושומע מפיו תורה

gloss_en: fear and shame (yir'ah u-vushah) — the paired experience of awe of God and shame at one's distance from Him, which together constitute the essence of repentance and are identified with Shabbat (via the Tikkunei Zohar anagram of Bereishit: 'fears shame / fears Shabbat')

Teshuvah Ila'ah — the kabbalistic 'higher/supernal repentance' (Aramaic ila'ah, 'upper'), the elevated level of return associated with Binah in Lurianic Kabbalah, here identified with the constriction of the throat (meitzar ha-garon) symbolized by Egypt; distinct from ordinary/lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah)

the Fiftieth Gate (Sha'ar HaChamishim) — the fiftieth gate of understanding/repentance beyond the forty-nine gates of teshuvah, identified with God's own 'return' (ve-ashuvah aleichem) at the giving of the Torah on the fiftieth day

the freedom (cherut) of Passover — the spiritual liberation from bondage/exile that Pesach embodies, toward which Purim (via Mordechai) is a path and preparation; not charut ('engraved,' as on the Tablets)
kedushah — holiness as a state/quality; here the sanctity in which eating and the tzaddik's presence are invested, distinct from mere separateness

canonical_he: נעשה המתקה, שלא יתגבר הצער ביותר
gloss_en: the sweetening effected through eating in holiness so that daily suffering (tza'ar) does not overwhelm — an act of hamtakah (mitigation of pain/judgment)
forms: נעשה המתקה, שלא יתגבר הצער ביותר

gloss_en: retzu'ah dikedushah — the 'strap of holiness': holy fear (yirah) figured as the tefillin strap, counterpart to the evil strap
retzu'ah bisha (Zohar, Intro 11b) — the 'evil strap': the demonic lash of fallen fear that inflicts suffering and judgment
yirah nefulah — fallen fear: awe of Heaven degraded into worldly fears/anxieties, identified with the evil strap

canonical_he: רצועה שעוברת בתוך המעברתא של תפלין
forms: רצועה שעוברת בתוך המעברתא של תפלין

canonical_he: ממתיק הצער והדין הבא מרצועה בישא
gloss_en: the act of sweetening/mitigating the suffering and judgment (din) that descends from the evil strap (retzu'ah bisha), accomplished via holy eating
forms: ממתיק הצער והדין הבא מרצועה בישא

gloss_en: the transformation whereby eating in holiness makes the mouth into the 'stature of Adam' (komat adam) — human, not animal, per 'Who placed a mouth for man' (Ex. 4:11)
the resulting state: the mouth rendered into komat adam (full human stature) by bringing Malkhut/fear into it during holy eating

canonical_he: שאוכל עם יראת־שמים, בקדשה ובטהרה כראוי
gloss_en: the practice of eating with fear of Heaven, in holiness and purity as is fitting — the devotional mode of eating that draws Malkhut into the mouth
forms: שאוכל עם יראת־שמים, בקדשה ובטהרה כראוי

gloss_en: matnat chinam — an unearned free gift; what Moshe requested via 'va-etchanan' (Deut. 3:23) in pleading to enter the Land of Israel
mitzvot zemaniyot — time-bound commandments, given so as to bind and elevate time itself into the aspect of above-time

canonical_he: שיתאחד הזמן ויעלה הזמן לבחינת למעלה מהזמן
gloss_en: the goal that time be unified and ascend into the aspect of above-time (lema'alah mehazman) — the essence of the avodah of nullifying time
forms: שיתאחד הזמן ויעלה הזמן לבחינת למעלה מהזמן

gloss_en: the hearing of the holy voice (kol dikedushah, the voice of Yaakov), attained through teshuvah/nullification of time
milchemet Amalek — the war against Amalek (Ex. 17), interpreted as teshuvah, fought while Moshe, Aharon and Chur fasted
Yitzchak son of Avraham — the patriarch Isaac as symbol of time (letters of 'keitz chai') born from Avraham who is above time
the unification of time achieved through teshuvah — time rising to be bound and included in the above-time realm
lema'alah min hazman — the supra-temporal realm/aspect above time, associated with Avraham's love, into which time is elevated
hit'achdut hazman — the unification of time itself: time becoming one, connected and included in the above-time
kolo yitbarakh — the voice of God Himself, the holy voice (voice of Yaakov) heard through teshuvah

canonical_he: זוכין לשמע קולו יתברך, הינו הקול דקדשה
gloss_en: the merited state of hearing His blessed voice, i.e., the kol dikedushah/voice of Yaakov, gained via teshuvah as nullification of time
forms: זוכין לשמע קולו יתברך, הינו הקול דקדשה

gloss_en: time (zman) — temporality itself, the created order of time that is bound up with sleep and the 'end of days,' and which teshuvah nullifies; not the verb זִמֵּן 'to summon/prepare' or זִמּוּן 'invitation'
keitz (קֵץ) — 'end,' the appointed end-point of time; the eschatological 'end of days' (as in 'mikeitz' and the anagram keitz chai within Yitzchak), signifying temporality itself
the shortening of time — the sun setting early for Yaakov ('ki va hashemesh'), an instance of time's nullification
bitul hazman — the nullification of time, equated with teshuvah; time annulled by absorption into the above-time

dibburim — spoken utterances/words of speech (plural of dibbur), the articulated speech formed from combinations of the twenty-two letters of the Torah; linked here to teshuvah via 'Take words with you and return' (Hosea 14:3) and to the stones/letters of 'avnei ha-makom'
kedushat hamachshavah — holiness/purity of thought ('merashotav'), the faculty that clarifies and repairs all blemishes, root of teshuvah's rectification
payis — the Temple lottery for assigning the ash-removal service (Yoma ch. 2), read as the enactment against pursuing leadership
yefaysu — the people's act of appeasing/entreating a person to accept leadership; only such conciliation legitimates exaltedness
hatzbi'u — 'extend fingers' read as a hint to intellect/attainment: displaying one's grasp (sikhlam) of Torah in the leadership contest
hatzbi'u — the Temple finger-count command ('extend one or two'), reinterpreted as the yetzer's incitement to display oneself for leadership

canonical_he: שיראה איזה צביעות בפני המון עם
gloss_en: tzevi'ut — showing off/hypocritical religious display before the masses in order to win leadership, the yetzer's counsel
forms: שיראה איזה צביעות בפני המון עם

gloss_en: the memuneh — the Temple official who runs the lottery, allegorized as the yetzer hara (evil inclination) inciting rivals

the kevesh — the inclined ramp ascending the Temple altar (כֶּבֶשׁ, Yoma ch. 2), which the priests ran up to win the terumat ha-deshen, homiletically linked to kivshono shel olam, the hidden secrets/depths of the world (Chagigah 13); NOT כֶּבֶשׂ 'lamb/sheep' and not the verb כָּבַשׁ 'to conquer/subdue'
kivshono shel olam — the 'hidden furnace/ramp of the world' (cf. Chagigah 13), the concealed divine mysteries; punned on the Temple ramp (kevesh) climbed by leadership-seekers

canonical_he: כל המדרגות התחתונות המכנים בשם רגלים, נתעלים
gloss_en: the elevation of all lower spiritual levels termed 'feet' (raglayim) through the joy of Torah and mitzvot
forms: כל המדרגות התחתונות המכנים בשם רגלים, נתעלים

gloss_en: the lower rungs/levels (madregot tachtonot) themselves — everything designated 'feet' in the cosmic stature awaiting elevation
dibbur hara — evil/slanderous speech, called 'regel' from 'lo ragal al leshono' (Ps. 15:3), also elevated by joy
the collective elevation of everything named 'foot' (regel) — speech, wealth, wife, lower levels — via mitzvah-joy that reaches the feet
kar'a — 'leg' (Aramaic): the wife as her husband's leg ('itto kar'a debala'), the regel elevated by rejoicing her in a mitzvah
the letter Heh — the letter symbolizing the wife/Malkhut ('raglei chasidav'), which joy raises and binds upward
Torah and mitzvah as a pair — the joy of whose performance ('tzedek yikra'ehu leraglo') elevates the feet/lower levels
supporters of the Torah (tomkhei de-oraita) — those who uphold/financially sustain Torah study, the Zoharic term for patrons of Torah scholars, identified with samkhei keshot ('supporters of truth')
samkhei keshot — 'supports of truth' (Zoharic term for Netzach and Hod, the leg-pillars), elevated to the heart through dance-joy
the elevation of all supporters of Torah (tomkhei de'oraita — those who uphold/fund Torah, the Netzach-Hod 'legs') through mitzvah-joy
prophets (נְבִיאִים) — the prophets as bearers of prophecy, identified kabbalistically with the sefirot Netzach and Hod, the 'legs' of the divine structure and the source of prophetic inspiration
the divine name YHVH spelled out with alefs (milui alfin) totaling 45 = MaH — the gematria linked to Adam (45), aspect of order (kesseder)

order / proper sequence (seder) — the state of things proceeding in their correct arrangement, as in the aleph-bet in its forward order (kesseder, 'kedem') versus reversed tashra"k (shelo kesseder, 'achor'); the divine flow received in order via the yud, whose disruption brings heart-sickness
achor — 'behind' of Psalms 139:5, symbol of the reversed order (tashrak alphabet), the not-in-sequence aspect linked to Chavah/Malkhut; not the body's back per se
tashrak — the alphabet recited in reverse order (tav-shin-resh-kuf), emblem of 'not in order' / achor
the alphabet in its proper forward order (aleph-bet-gimel...), the sequential arrangement of the Hebrew letters from aleph onward, as opposed to the reversed tashrak order

shleimut — completeness/wholeness (שְׁלֵמוּת): the perfected, undeficient state of a thing, attained only when it is unified and bound to God; identified with fullness (milui) and vitality (chiyut), whose absence in a limb is called a deficiency (chisaron)
milui — fullness/completion of a thing, identified with its vitality (chiyut); the state of being whole through connection to God, not a letter-filling spelling
dalet-vav-yud — the letters of the spelled-out yud (yu"d), Chokhmah's vitality drawn into Malkhut-dalet; a letter-filling, not 'illness' (dvai)
kaf — the letter kaf as numerical value 20, from the al-tikrei reading of 'kapekha' (Ps 139:5), equal to yud's gematria doubled into Malkhut
the letter dalet — letter-symbol of Malkhut who 'has nothing of her own' (dal, poor) until receiving the yud of Chokhmah
a thing drawn down from a high place — an occurrence whose root is in an exalted supernal source, which therefore may arrive below 'not in order'
shevi — the captivity/captive of Deut 21:10 ('and you take its captives'), the opposing will taken captive and subdued in the inner war
binding His divinity into your thought — the contemplative act of attaching awareness of God to one's mind during opposition

canonical_he: יתבטלו כל המלחמות וכל הרצונות נגד רצונך
gloss_en: the nullification of all wars and all wills opposing your will — the promised state of 'Hashem delivers him into your hand'
forms: יתבטלו כל המלחמות וכל הרצונות נגד רצונך

gloss_en: milchamah — war defined as opposition of wills, the existential aspect of 'not in order'; the war of Deut 21:10 read inwardly
his blood is spilled — suffering shame/humiliation as literal bloodshed (the blood draining from the face), functioning as slaughter of the self
zera merei'im — 'seed of evildoers' (Isaiah 1:4), the corrupt brood/external passions assailing the heart, akin to the flood-waters
the waters of the Flood (mabul) — archetype of the overwhelming 'many waters' of alien loves and fears
mayim rabbim — the 'many waters' of Song 8:7 that cannot quench love: external loves and fears threatening the heart's holy ardor
external loves and fears — fallen, outward ahavot and yir'ot (the 'many waters') opposed to holy love and awe of God
shin — the letter shin of 'Shabbat' (shin + bat), whose three strokes signify the three elements fire, wind, water
fire, wind, water — the three primal elements (telat gevanin) symbolized by the three heads of the letter shin
the holy body from the Garden of Eden — the pure 'Shabbat-garment' body donned after stripping the leprous serpent-skin body
the fallen souls — souls that have no ascent except through the spilled blood (shaming/martyrdom) of Israel
kisui ha-dam — the ritual covering of blood, read as the Shekhinah covering Israel's blood spilled through shame borne in love
shefikhut damim — spilling of blood: shame/humiliation as bloodshed serving as the 'shechitah' that permits the tzaddik's mitzvot to be 'tasted'
the holiness of Shabbat — identified with 'the ultimate of knowing is that we do not know,' the takhlit of heaven and earth
the three vavs — 3×6=18, the chai (eighteen) blessings of the Amidah as 'arrows' shot from the bow of the rectified brit
connection and cleaving (devekut) to God — the essential attachment to the Blessed One attained through the gate of prayer
the renewal of the oath to the Patriarchs — the sworn covenant to the Avot reawakened/re-established through prayer's power
the rectification (tikkun) of the Shekhinah — restoring Malkhut from her darkened exile state
the upholding/establishing of the covenant (brit) — making the brit stand firm, linked to 'u-vriti ne'emenet lo'
eshet chayil — the 'Woman of Valor' (Proverbs 31) as a name of Malkhut to be rectified through the strength God gives
'you shall rectify the eshet chayil' — the act of repairing Malkhut through the koach (strength) of Deut 8:18, read as la'asot chayil
his shoulders — the shoulders as anatomical locus in the partzuf-scheme, the region behind/below the neck associated with Leah at the oref
the aspect of Leah — the first nukva (feminine partzuf) positioned at the oref (back of the head/neck), alluded to by luzim-nuts
the aspect of Rachel — the second, lower feminine partzuf, counterpart to Leah of the oref
beitzah — an egg, the enclosed shell-covered form likened to the nut/luz in this imagery of hidden inner content
Beit El — the place Jacob named 'House of God' (identified with the Temple), entered by way of the city Luz
entering the Beit HaMikdash — the act of coming into the Holy Temple (Beit El) by first passing through Luz/Leah
nuts called luzim — the egozim/luz-nuts (hazelnuts) whose name alludes to the city Luz and to Leah at the oref
the oref — the back of the neck / nape (anatomical rear of the head, kabbalistically the locus of Leah, the first feminine aspect, associated with the kodkod and the gateway to Beit El)
the luz tree (hazel/almond tree, ilan luz) whose nuts (egozim/luzim) symbolize Leah at the back of the neck and the town Luz as gateway to Beit El — in Likutey Moharan II:85

Luz — the nut called 'luz' (hazelnut/almond) homiletically identified with the biblical city Luz, the gateway through which one enters Beit El; symbolizing Leah, the first feminine aspect located at the back of the neck (oref/kodkod)

the luz bone — the indestructible almond-shaped bone at the nape of the neck (oref/kodkod) from which the body is rebuilt at the resurrection of the dead; linked to Leah at the back of the neck and to the city Luz as gateway to Beit El
the essence of our consolation — the core nechamah, rooted in 'nachamu nachamu' whose double gematria equals kodkod (crown of the head)
Shabbat Nachamu — the Sabbath after Tisha B'Av when Isaiah 40:1 'Nachamu nachamu' is read, Shabbat of consolation
ma'arikh rucho — patiently extending one's spirit: forbearing endurance in divine service, the counterpart to needing harsh fasts
ketanei amanah — 'those of little faith': the spiritual state/category of people deficient in emunah, whose weak faith necessitates fasting and harsh devotions
ketzar ruach — 'shortness of spirit/breath': the state of impatience and constricted spirit (cf. Exodus 6:9) stemming from little faith, opposite of patient, expansive breath of emunah
"af ein yesh ruach bahem" — verse fragment (Habakkuk 2:19/Jeremiah 10:14, of idols) 'there is no breath/spirit in them,' cited as prooftext for absence of ruach/spirit linked to faithlessness
kavvanat Elul — the Arizal's kabbalistic meditative intentions for the month of Elul, keyed to 'He who makes a path in the sea' (Isaiah 43:16), functioning as tikkun for the blemished covenant

canonical_he: מוצא זווגו, והיא אינה כנגדו, רק כרצונו
gloss_en: finding one's zivug (destined marriage partner) such that she is not 'against him' (a menagedet, opponent) but rather in accord with his will — the restored-match state achieved via tikkun ha-brit
forms: מוצא זווגו, והיא אינה כנגדו, רק כרצונו

gloss_en: the Elul kavvanot as the specific tikkun (rectification) for pegam ha-brit — the secret Avraham transmitted to Eliezer when sending him to find Yitzchak's match
the reversal whereby desire toward him is re-created in her — the restored ratzon of the destined bride toward her partner effected by tikkun ha-brit/Elul kavvanot
the remedial action of coming to the bar-da'at (the man of Da'at, the tzaddik) to hear Torah directly from his mouth — the means of finding one's shidduch
the resulting capacity to find one's shidduch (marriage match) — outcome of hearing Torah from the bar-da'at, since Da'at mediates the two opposites of every match
the customary breaking of an earthenware (clay) vessel at the time of an engagement match (tena'im/shidduch), whose reason Rabbi Nachman expounds
Sha'ar ha-Charsit — the 'Pottery/Potsherd Gate' (Jeremiah 19:2, gate facing Gei Ben-Hinnom), place-name invoked in the symbolism of breaking a clay vessel at an engagement
Gei Ben-Hinnom — the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, the toponym underlying 'Gehinnom' (purgatory), linked to the bad-wife teaching of Eruvin 41b and the broken clay vessel

the opening (entrance) of Gehinnom — the gateway through which one enters purgatory, invoked in Likutey Moharan II:90 as the aspect symbolized by breaking a clay vessel at an engagement (since accepting a bad wife with love spares one from seeing the face of Gehinnom)
hitkashrut — the act of truly binding/attaching oneself to true tzaddikim, which yields complete teshuvah, atonement, sweetening of judgments, and the unification of the Holy One and His Shekhinah
mi'ut ha-levanah — the kabbalistic 'diminishment of the moon': Malkhut/Lower Wisdom shrunken when worldly wisdoms separate from Torah, synonymous with the exile of the Shekhinah
the totality of the holy Torah identified as Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom) — Torah as the supernal wisdom from which all lower worldly wisdoms derive

the exile of the Shekhinah — the kabbalistic state in which the Divine Presence (Shekhinah, identified with Lower Wisdom / Malkhut) is estranged and cut off from its divine source, as when worldly wisdoms are severed from Torah and God (paralleling the diminishing of the moon)
the filling of the moon's blemish (pegimat ha-levanah) — restoration of diminished Malkhut/Lower Wisdom, read from Targum on 'the wisdom of Shlomo increased' (I Kings 5)

canonical_he: נמתקין כל הדינים ונתכפרין כל העוונות
gloss_en: the sweetening/nullification of all judgments (dinim) and atonement of all sins — the effect when the two 'kings'/wisdoms unite and the moon's blemish is filled (Zohar Vayigash)
forms: נמתקין כל הדינים ונתכפרין כל העוונות

canonical_he: שהצדיק מלביש אור התורה בספורי דברים
gloss_en: the tzaddik's act of clothing (halbashah) the light of Torah in mundane stories/conversation — garbing Upper Wisdom in narrative so lower minds can receive it
forms: שהצדיק מלביש אור התורה בספורי דברים

canonical_he: מקשר חכמה תתאה עם חכמה עלאה
gloss_en: the tzaddik's function of binding Chokhmah Tata'ah (Lower Wisdom/Malkhut) with Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom) — the coupling that unites the two worlds
forms: מקשר חכמה תתאה עם חכמה עלאה

gloss_en: leimor (לֵאמֹר, 'saying') — the biblical infinitive 'to say' as homiletically read in LM II:91 as a term of clothing/garment (from emrah = garment, per 'bitza emrato'), signifying the tzaddik's clothing of Torah light in stories and words
halbashah — 'enclothement': the kabbalistic mechanism of garbing a higher light (Torah/Upper Wisdom) within lower garments (stories, worldly speech)
'et' (אֵת) — the accusative particle in 'Vayedaber Elokim et,' read as a symbol of Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom), as in 'et hashamayim'
'Vayedaber' ('And He spoke,' Exodus 20:1) — the word read as a term of zivug (coupling/connection), per 'they saw her medaberet' (Ketubot 13a)

"li" (לִי, 'for Me') — the word from Psalms 94:16 'Who will rise up for Me (li) against evildoers,' cited in Sotah 13b at Moshe's death, homiletically decomposed into its letters lamed and yud, signifying the bond of Lower Wisdom and Upper Wisdom that the tzaddik effects
the paired kabbalistic terms Chokhmah Ila'ah and Chokhmah Tata'ah — Upper Wisdom (Torah/supernal world) and Lower Wisdom (Malkhut/worldly wisdoms), the two worlds whose union the tzaddik effects

the letter-pair Lamed–Yud that spells the word לִי ("for Me") in "מִי יָקוּם לִי עִם מְרֵעִים", expounded as the joining of the letter Lamed (alluding to Upper Wisdom, chokhmah ila'ah) with the letter Yod (alluding to Lower Wisdom, chokhmah tata'ah) — the union effected by the true tzaddik; not the verb לָמַד ("he learned")
the student learning from the master — the rav–talmid relation as the model for how Chokhmah Tata'ah suckles and receives from Chokhmah Ila'ah
the Ten Kinds of Melody (asarah minei neginah — Berakhah, Ashrei, Maskil, etc.) with which the Book of Psalms was composed, the power basis of the Tikkun HaKlali
tikkun le-mikreh lailah — the rectification for a nocturnal seminal emission: reciting the ten psalms (Tikkun HaKlali) corresponding to the ten kinds of melody
mocho ve-da'ato — the tzaddik's brain/mind and consciousness, one of the 'heads' (rosh) that gather on Rosh Hashanah when one is with the tzaddik
go'el — 'redeemer': the kinsman-redeemer role (Boaz with Ruth), keyed to the secret of joining ge'ulah (redemption blessing) to tefillah (prayer)
the practice of innovating a novel Torah insight (chiddush) in the Rebbe's teachings — the act Rabbi Nachman urged his followers to attempt when studying his Torah
a great tikkun for hirhurim — the rectification of illicit/stray thoughts effected by innovating chiddushim in Torah
'he will see / will be seen' (verb from ראה, seeing — associated with direct light, or ha-yashar)
son (Aramaic), as in the dictum 'b'ra kar'a d'avuha' — the son is the leg of his father
field (poetic form of שָׂדֶה), as in 'ziz sadai' — the creature/bird of the field (Ps. 50:11), here darshened as the Supernal Unification
profit/gain (revach), monetary earnings figuratively termed 'birth'
